definition_zh: 无限；无穷；无限的空间；无穷远；极多
definition_en: the state of having no end or limit, or an amount that cannot be counted
core_image: 一条笔直延伸的路，看不到尽头，也数不到终点
scene: 孩子仰头追问天边之外还有什么，大人摊开双手表示无法给出终点。The child kept asking what lay beyond the horizon, and infinity was the only honest answer.
sceneCN: 这里 infinity 是「无限；无穷」（第 1 个义项：没有止境或极限的状态）；句意：孩子不断追问地平线之外有什么，而「无限」是唯一诚实的回答。

collocations.zh: 无限远处之外；比无穷更远
无穷符号（形似横放的数字八）

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 infinitus 借入，义为「无限的；无穷的」
由 infinite 加拉丁词尾 -esimal 构成，义为「极微小的；无穷小的」
由 infinite 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「无限地；极其」
由拉丁语 finitus 派生，义为「有限性；有尽」

senses.title: The state of having no limit
senses.definition: the state of being without any end or limit
senses.definitionCN: 没有终点或极限的状态
senses.example: The philosopher asked whether time could have an infinity of changes.
senses.exampleCN: 这位哲学家追问时间能否容纳无穷的变化。
senses.why: Latin in- means not and finis means end, so infinity is literally the condition of having no boundary.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 in- 表示「不」，finis 表示「边界」，所以无限就是「没有边界」的状态。

senses.title: Endless space or time
senses.definition: space or time that stretches on with no possible end
senses.definitionCN: 看不到尽头、不可能结束的空间或时间
senses.example: He stared into the infinity of the night sky.
senses.exampleCN: 他凝望着夜空的无限深远。
senses.why: When the abstract condition is pictured as a place, the word names an endless expanse.
senses.whyCN: 当「无边界」被想象成一个地方时，这个词就指一片没有尽头的广阔空间。

senses.title: A number larger than any given amount
senses.definition: a mathematical quantity that is larger than any finite number
senses.definitionCN: 数学中比任何有限数都大的量
senses.example: The function tends to infinity as the value approaches zero.
senses.exampleCN: 当取值趋近于零时，这个函数趋于无穷大。
senses.why: Mathematics turns the idea of no end into a precise symbol that can be used in equations.
senses.whyCN: 数学把「没有尽头」转化为一个可以写进方程的精确符号。

senses.title: An extremely large quantity
senses.definition: a very great number or amount far too large to count
senses.definitionCN: 数量极多、根本数不完的数目或数量
senses.example: An infinity of tiny stars filled the telescope view.
senses.exampleCN: 无穷多的小星星布满望远镜的视野。
senses.why: In everyday speech the word is used loosely for a quantity so large that counting seems pointless.
senses.whyCN: 日常口语里这个词用来泛指多到不必去数的数量，是从「无边界」引申出的夸张说法。

senses.title: A very distant point or range
senses.definition: a point or distance so far away that it lies beyond any practical limit
senses.definitionCN: 远到超出任何实际限度、仿佛无穷远的距离或范围
senses.example: In the photograph the road narrows to a point at infinity.
senses.exampleCN: 照片中那条路一直收窄成无穷远处的一个点。
senses.why: Art and geometry place the end of sight at infinity, turning no end into a far-off focus.
senses.whyCN: 绘画与几何把视线的尽头放在「无穷远」，于是「没有终点」变成了一个遥远的聚焦点。

intro.en: Infinity comes from Latin infinitas, the quality of having no end, built on in- meaning not and finis meaning end.
intro.cn: infinity 来自拉丁语 infinitas（没有尽头的性质），由 in-（不）与 finis（边界、终点）构成。

items.en: A reconstructed root related to boundary underlies Latin finis.
items.cn: 拉丁语 finis 可追溯到表示「边界」的原始印欧语词根（重构形式）。

items.en: Finis means end or boundary, and in- means not.
items.cn: finis 意为终点或边界，in- 意为不。

items.en: Infinitas names the state of having no end.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 infinitas 指没有尽头的状态。

items.en: Infinité carries the sense of unbounded extent into French.
items.cn: 古法语 infinité 承载「无边无际」的意思进入法语。

items.en: Infynyte and infinity appear in English for the endless.
items.cn: 中古英语已出现 infynyte、infinity，表示没有尽头。

items.en: Mathematics gives infinity a symbol and a technical role.
items.cn: 现代数学给 infinity 配上专用符号，使其成为技术概念。

note.en: Infinity is the noun form of endlessness, connected to infinite, infinitesimal, and nearer ideas like endlessness and boundlessness.
note.cn: infinity 是表示「没有尽头」的名词，与 infinite、infinitesimal 同族，与「无尽」「无边」等概念相邻。

normalIntro.en: Infinity is built from in- meaning not and finis meaning end, so it is the state of having no end at all.
normalIntro.cn: infinity 由 in-（不）和 finis（终点）构成，字面就是「没有终点」的状态。

normal.en: Finis is Latin for the end, as in the final line of a play.
normal.cn: finis 是拉丁语的「终点」，剧本最后一行常写它就是「剧终」。

normal.en: The prefix in- simply says not, so infinity means no end.
normal.cn: 前缀 in- 表示「不」，所以 infinity 就是「没有终点」。

normal.en: Words in the same family share the root: finite, final, finish, define.
normal.cn: 填写、终结这些感觉相同：finite、final、finish、define 都含「边界」词根。

normal.en: The infinity symbol looks like an upright eight turned on its side.
normal.cn: infinity 的符号像一个横躺的数字八，绕一圈又回来，仿佛没有起点也没有终点。

normal.en: To infinity means without any stopping, as in a road that runs forever.
normal.cn: to infinity 表示「一直到底、没有停」，像一条永远延伸的路。

abstract.en: Picture a single light in a dark hall that keeps going after the wall is gone.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗大厅里的一束光，穿墙之后还在继续延伸。

abstract.en: Imagine counting upward and never being able to say the last number.
abstract.cn: 想象一直往上数数，永远说不出最后一个数。

abstract.en: Think of a track where every lap of a race simply loops back with no finish line.
abstract.cn: 想一条赛跑跑道，每圈都绕回原处，却没有终点线。

examples.en: Mathematicians use the infinity symbol to stand for a number beyond all others.
examples.cn: 数学家使用无穷符号来表示比任何数都大的量。

examples.en: She felt a sense of infinity looking across the desert at night.
examples.cn: 夜里望着沙漠，她体会到一种无边的感觉。

examples.en: The sequence continues toward infinity without ever stopping.
examples.cn: 这个序列不断趋向无穷，永远不会停止。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因非你体」——因为不是有限的身体，所以可以无限延伸；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ finis（边界、终点）→ 晚期拉丁语 infinitas → 英语 infinity，核心义「没有边界」。

sensesIntro.en: Infinity moves from the abstract state of no boundary, to endless space, to a mathematical quantity, to a very large number, and finally to a distant point.
sensesIntro.cn: infinity 从「没有边界」的抽象状态出发，延伸到无垠的空间、数学中的无穷大、极多的数量，最后落到无穷远的一点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a straight road that runs on past every visible landmark.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条笔直的路，越过所有可见的路标仍不结束。

branches.en: The abstract state of having no limit is the core sense.
branches.cn: 「没有边界」的抽象状态是核心义项。

branches.en: Endless space or time is the condition pictured as an expanse.
branches.cn: 无垠的空间或时间是把状态想象成一片广阔。

branches.en: A mathematical value larger than any number is the technical sense.
branches.cn: 数学上比任何数都大的量是技术义项。

branches.en: An uncountable amount is the everyday exaggeration of having no end.
branches.cn: 极多的数量是日常口语对「没有终点」的夸张说法。

branches.en: A far point at infinity is endless space collapsed into one remote focus.
branches.cn: 无穷远的一点是无垠空间收缩成的那个遥远焦点。

intro.en: Infinity is built from a Latin negative prefix and the root for end, with infinite and infinitesimal around it.
intro.cn: infinity 由拉丁语否定前缀与「终点」词根构成，英语围绕它形成 infinite、infinitesimal 等词。

latinIntro.en: Latin in- means not and finis means end or boundary, giving infinitas, the state of having no end.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 in- 意为「不」，finis 意为「终点、边界」，两者合成为 infinitas，即「没有尽头」。

items.example: The prefix in- reverses the meaning of the root.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 把词根的意思反转为否定。

items.example: Finis gives the idea of a limit.
items.exampleCN: finis 提供「限度」的概念。

items.example: Infinitus describes something without a boundary.
items.exampleCN: infinitus 描述没有边界的东西。

items.example: Infinitas is the direct source of the noun.
items.exampleCN: infinitas 是这个名词的直接来源。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ity turns the adjective into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 把形容词变成名词。

items.example: Infinite space is without a boundary.
items.exampleCN: infinite 表示空间没有边界。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms infinitely.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 infinitely。

items.example: The suffix -esimal forms infinitesimal.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -esimal 构成 infinitesimal。

items.example: Finite keeps the root meaning of a boundary.
items.exampleCN: finite 保留「边界」的词根含义。

definition_zh: 体弱；虚弱；疾病；弱点；缺陷
definition_en: weakness of body or mind, or a particular illness or failing
core_image: 一位老人扶着墙慢慢挪步，双腿发软，站不太稳
scene: 老人扶着栏杆一级一级走上楼梯，走几步就要停下来喘气。Years of infirmity had made the stairs feel like a mountain to him.
sceneCN: 这里 infirmity 是「体弱；虚弱」（第 1 个义项：身体虚弱、缺乏力气）；句意：多年的体弱让他觉得这几级楼梯像一座山。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 infirmus 借入，义为「体弱的；虚弱的」
与 infirmity 共含「坚固」词根，义为「结实的；坚定的」
由 infirm 加表示场所的后缀 -ary 构成，义为「医务室；疗养院」

senses.title: Weakness of the body
senses.definition: the condition of being weak and lacking physical strength
senses.definitionCN: 身体虚弱、缺少力气的状态
senses.example: The injury left him with a lasting infirmity in one leg.
senses.exampleCN: 那次受伤让他的腿留下了长期的虚弱。
senses.why: Latin in- means not and firmus means firm, so infirmity is quite literally being not firm.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 in- 表示「不」，firmus 表示「坚固」，所以体弱字面上就是「不坚固、站不稳」。

senses.title: A particular illness
senses.definition: a specific disease or chronic ailment that weakens someone
senses.definitionCN: 使人体弱的具体疾病或慢性病痛
senses.example: The doctor asked about every infirmity she had suffered in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 医生问起她冬天得过的每一种病。
senses.why: A lasting illness is the concrete form that the abstract weakness takes in one body.
senses.whyCN: 长期的疾病就是抽象的「虚弱」在具体身体上表现出的样子。

senses.title: Weakness of mind or character
senses.definition: a moral or mental weakness, a failing in character
senses.definitionCN: 道德或精神上的弱点，性格上的缺陷
senses.example: He blamed his own infirmity for giving way to anger again.
senses.exampleCN: 他责怪自己意志薄弱，又一次发火了。
senses.why: The image of an unsteady body is transferred to the mind, which also can lose its firm footing.
senses.whyCN: 身体站不稳的画面被挪到心灵上，因为意志同样会失去稳固的立足点。

senses.title: A flaw in something abstract
senses.definition: a weakness or weakness-like flaw in a plan, system, or argument
senses.definitionCN: 计划、制度或论证中的薄弱之处或缺陷
senses.example: The report points out the infirmity of an argument resting on guesswork.
senses.exampleCN: 报告指出了建立在猜测之上的论证的薄弱之处。
senses.why: Anything firm can be tested for stability, so the word extends from people to institutions and ideas.
senses.whyCN: 凡是坚固的东西都可以检验其稳固性，所以这个词从人延伸到制度与观点。

intro.en: Infirmity comes from Latin infirmitas, from infirmus meaning not strong, built on in- meaning not and firmus meaning firm.
intro.cn: infirmity 来自拉丁语 infirmitas，源于 infirmus（不坚固的），由 in-（不）与 firmus（坚固）构成。

items.en: Latin firmus is generally linked to a reconstructed root meaning to hold firm.
items.cn: 拉丁语 firmus 一般认为可追溯到表示「牢固支撑」的原始印欧语词根（重构形式）。

items.en: Firmus means firm or steady, and in- makes infirmus, not firm.
items.cn: firmus 意为坚固、稳当，加上 in- 便成 infirmus（不坚固）。

items.en: Infirmitas names weakness of body or spirit.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 infirmitas 指身体或精神的虚弱。

items.en: Enfermeté carries the sense of illness into French.
items.cn: 古法语 enfermeté 把「病弱」的意思带入法语。

items.en: Infirmite appears in Middle English for sickness and weakness.
items.cn: 中古英语 infirmite 表示疾病与虚弱。

items.en: Modern usage extends the word from the body to character and institutions.
items.cn: 现代用法把该词从身体扩展到性格与制度。

note.en: Infirmity is the noun of not being firm, linked to infirm, firm, and to near ideas such as frailty and weakness.
note.cn: infirmity 是「不坚固」的名词形式，与 infirm、firm 同根，与 frailty、weakness 等表示虚弱的概念相邻。

entries.definition: physically or mentally weak
solid and steady
a place for the sick or injured
physical or moral weakness
an illness that is not very serious

normalIntro.en: Infirmity is the noun of infirm, and infirm is simply in- plus firm, so the word literally means not firm.
normalIntro.cn: infirmity 是 infirm 的名词，而 infirm 就是 in- 加 firm，字面意思是「不坚固」。

normal.en: Think of a firm stance and then take away the firmness with in-.
normal.cn: 先想一个站稳的站姿，再用 in- 把「稳」拿走。

normal.en: The same firm root appears in confirm and affirm, where it means making something solid.
normal.cn: 同一个 firm 词根也出现在 confirm 与 affirm 中，表示使某事变得牢靠。

normal.en: An infirmary is a room for the infirm, so the adjective came first.
normal.cn: infirmary（医务室）是给 infirm（体弱者）用的房间，说明形容词在先。

normal.en: Infirmity often follows old age in writing, as in the phrase old age and infirmity.
normal.cn: 书面语中 infirmity 常与年老搭配，例如年老体弱。

normal.en: The plural infirmities is used for several ailments or failings at once.
normal.cn: 复数 infirmities 用来一次指好几种病痛或缺点。

abstract.en: Picture a walking stick that bends under every step.
abstract.cn: 想象一根拐杖每走一步都弯一下。

abstract.en: Imagine a wall that shakes whenever a hand rests on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一面墙，手一搭上去就晃动。

abstract.en: Think of a bridge with one loose plank that everyone steps around.
abstract.cn: 想一座桥，其中一块木板松动，人人绕开它走。

examples.en: He retired early because of a long infirmity that kept him out of work.
examples.cn: 他因长期体弱而无法工作，所以提前退休了。

examples.en: The family checked on the old man each day, fearing his infirmity would worsen.
examples.cn: 家人每天去看望老人，担心他的病弱会加重。

examples.en: Critics noted the infirmity of a plan built on weak evidence.
examples.cn: 评论者指出，这个建立在薄弱证据上的计划存在缺陷。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因肺门体」——因肺门虚弱而体弱，容易联想到体弱多病；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ firmus（坚固）→ infirmus（不坚固的）→ infirmitas → 英语 infirmity，核心义「不够坚固」。

sensesIntro.en: Infirmity starts as a bodily weakness, moves to a specific illness, then to a weakness of character, and finally to a flaw in an abstract thing.
sensesIntro.cn: infirmity 先指身体的虚弱，再指具体的病痛，接着指性格上的弱点，最后指抽象事物的缺陷。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body that cannot keep itself steady.
core.cn: 核心意象：一副稳不住的身体。

branches.en: Bodily weakness is the literal sense of not being firm.
branches.cn: 身体虚弱是「不坚固」的字面义项。

branches.en: An illness is the lasting cause of that weakness.
branches.cn: 疾病是造成那种虚弱的长期原因。

branches.en: Weakness of character transfers the unsteady body to the mind.
branches.cn: 性格薄弱是把不稳的身体迁移到心上。

branches.en: Weakness and illness often appear together, as in old age and infirmity.
branches.cn: 虚弱与疾病常同时出现，如年老体弱。

branches.en: A moral failing and a flawed plan are both weak points.
branches.cn: 道德上的弱点和计划的缺陷都是「薄弱之处」。

intro.en: Infirmity is built on the negative prefix in- and the root firm, which also lives in firm, infirm, and infirmary.
intro.cn: infirmity 由否定前缀 in- 与词根 firm 构成，这个词根也活在 firm、infirm、infirmary 中。

latinIntro.en: Latin firmus means firm, and with in- meaning not it forms infirmus, the state of being infirm is infirmitas.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 firmus 意为坚固，加上表示「不」的 in- 成为 infirmus，其状态名词为 infirmitas。

items.example: The prefix in- makes the adjective negative.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 使形容词变成否定。

items.example: Firmus supplies the idea of solidity.
items.exampleCN: firmus 提供「结实」的概念。

items.example: Infirmus describes the body that cannot stand steady.
items.exampleCN: infirmus 描述站不稳的身体。

items.example: Infirmitas is the direct source of the noun.
items.exampleCN: infirmitas 是这个名词的直接来源。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ity forms a noun of state.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成表示状态的名词。

items.example: Firm keeps the positive root meaning.
items.exampleCN: firm 保留词根的正面含义。

items.example: Infirm is the adjective behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: infirm 是这个名词背后的形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ary forms infirmary.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ary 构成 infirmary。

items.example: Confirm shares the root meaning of making firm.
items.exampleCN: confirm 共享「使坚固」的词根含义。

definition_zh: 使燃烧；激起；使愤怒；使发炎；使激动
definition_en: to excite strong feelings, to make a situation worse, or to make part of the body red and sore
core_image: 一根火柴划过，火苗一下子窜起来，越烧越旺
scene: 演讲者用尖锐的言辞点燃台下听众的情绪，人群中响起此起彼伏的喊声。Sharp words from the speaker began to inflame the crowd.
sceneCN: 这里 inflame 是「激起；使激动」（第 2 个义项：激起强烈的情绪）；句意：演讲者尖锐的言辞开始让台下人群的情绪激昂起来。

derivatives.zh: 由 inflame 加拉丁名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「炎症；发炎」
由本词加形容词后缀 -atory 构成，义为「炎症的；煽动性的」
由本词加形容词后缀 -able 构成，义为「易燃的；易激动的」
与 inflame 共含「火焰」词根，义为「火焰」

senses.title: To set something burning
senses.definition: to cause something to catch fire and burn
senses.definitionCN: 使某物着火、燃烧
senses.example: A spark can inflame the dry grass in seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 一个火星就能让干草瞬间燃烧起来。
senses.why: The word is built on the Latin root for flame, and the prefix in- adds the sense of setting something alight.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在拉丁语表示「火焰」的词根上，前缀 in- 又增添了「使…起火」的意思。

senses.title: To excite strong feelings
senses.definition: to make someone feel a strong emotion such as anger or passion
senses.definitionCN: 使某人产生愤怒、激情等强烈情绪
senses.example: His speech began to inflame the students with hope.
senses.exampleCN: 他的演讲开始让学生们满怀希望、情绪激昂。
senses.why: When a fire spreads in the mind rather than in wood, the same word describes rising emotion.
senses.whyCN: 火不在木头上烧而在心里烧时，同一个词便用来描述情绪的升腾。

senses.title: To make a bad situation worse
senses.definition: to strengthen a conflict or tension rather than calm it
senses.definitionCN: 使冲突或紧张局势加强，而不是缓和
senses.example: The comment only served to inflame the dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 那句话只是让争端烧得更旺。
senses.why: A fire that is fed instead of put out grows larger, so the word also means worsening a conflict.
senses.whyCN: 火被添柴而不是扑灭就会变大，所以这个词也指让冲突越闹越凶。

senses.title: To become red and sore
senses.definition: to make part of the body red, hot, and painful as a reaction to injury or infection
senses.definitionCN: 使身体某部位因受伤或感染而红肿发热、疼痛
senses.example: The bite may inflame the skin around it.
senses.exampleCN: 这次叮咬可能使周围的皮肤发炎。
senses.why: Old medical theory described inflammation as a kind of inner fire, the redness and heat of a flame.
senses.whyCN: 古代医学把炎症说成体内的一团火，红肿发热正如火焰的形态。

senses.title: To fill with desire
senses.definition: to make someone feel a strong desire, often a romantic one
senses.definitionCN: 使人产生强烈的欲望，尤指爱慕之情
senses.example: Her words were enough to inflame his curiosity.
senses.exampleCN: 她的话足以燃起他的好奇心。
senses.why: Passion is the most personal version of the inner fire, so the word also describes desire flaring up.
senses.whyCN: 激情是内心之火最私人的一面，所以这个词也用来描述欲望被点燃。

intro.en: Inflame comes from Latin inflammare, to set on fire, built on in- and flamma, a flame.
intro.cn: inflame 来自拉丁语 inflammare（点燃、使燃烧），由 in- 与 flamma（火焰）构成。

items.en: Latin flamma is generally linked to a reconstructed root related to burning.
items.cn: 拉丁语 flamma 一般认为可追溯到与「燃烧」相关的原始印欧语词根（重构形式）。

items.en: Flamma means flame, and inflammare means to set on fire.
items.cn: flamma 意为火焰，inflammare 意为点燃。

items.en: Enflamer carries the burning sense into French.
items.cn: 古法语 enflamer 把「燃烧」的意思带入法语。

items.en: Enflamen and later inflame appear in English.
items.cn: 中古英语先有 enflamen，后作 inflame。

items.en: The word takes on medical and emotional meanings.
items.cn: 该词逐渐获得医学上的「发炎」与情感上的「激怒」用法。

items.en: Inflame is now mostly figurative or medical, while the physical verb gives way to light and ignite.
items.cn: 现代英语中 inflame 多用于比喻与医学，表示分具体的「点火」时多用 light 与 ignite。

note.en: Inflame shares the flame root with flame, flammable, and inflammation, and stands near provoke, aggravate, and ignite.
note.cn: inflame 与 flame、flammable、inflammation 同含「火焰」词根，与 provoke、aggravate、ignite 等词意义相邻。

entries.definition: redness and swelling in part of the body
causing anger or swelling
able to catch fire easily
to cause anger or a reaction
to make a bad situation worse
to set fire to something

normalIntro.en: Inflame holds the Latin flame root flamma, so every sense keeps a picture of fire.
normalIntro.cn: inflame 含有拉丁语「火焰」词根 flamma，所以每个义项都藏着火的画面。

normal.en: The Latin noun flamma means flame, and English flame is its direct cousin.
normal.cn: 拉丁语名词 flamma 意为火焰，英语 flame 就是它的近亲。

normal.en: The prefix in- adds a sense of causing, so inflame is causing a flame.
normal.cn: 前缀 in- 带来「使之」的意思，所以 inflame 就是「使之燃起来」。

normal.en: Inflammable looks like it might mean not flammable, but it actually means catches fire easily.
normal.cn: inflammable 看起来像「不易燃」，其实意思正好相反，是「易燃的」。

normal.en: The noun of state is inflammation, formed with the suffix -ation.
normal.cn: 表示状态的名词是 inflammation，由后缀 -ation 构成。

normal.en: Inflammable and inflammatory both start with the same seven letters as inflame.
normal.cn: inflammable 与 inflammatory 都以与 inflame 相同的开头字母组构成，词族一眼可辨。

abstract.en: Picture a spark touching dry grass and running along it in a line of light.
abstract.cn: 想象一个火星碰到干草，化作一条亮线窜过去。

abstract.en: See a crowd whose faces turn red and angry as a speaker raises his voice.
abstract.cn: 想象演讲者抬高嗓门，人群的脸一张张变红发怒。

abstract.en: Feel a wound that grows hot and red when someone touches it.
abstract.cn: 感受一处伤口，被碰到就发烫发红。

examples.en: The new tax proposal is likely to inflame public anger.
examples.cn: 新的税收提案很可能激起公众的愤怒。

examples.en: Rubbing the sore spot will only inflame it further.
examples.cn: 揉搓那块疼痛的地方只会让它更红肿。

examples.en: Such careless remarks can inflame an already tense meeting.
examples.cn: 这种漫不经心的话会让本就紧张的会议更僵。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「引弗蕾姆」——把一线火苗引进来，让它烧起来；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（使）+ flamma（火焰）→ inflammare（点燃）→ 古法语 enflamer → 英语 inflame，核心义「使燃烧」。

sensesIntro.en: Inflame begins with setting something on fire, then moves to excited feelings, to worsening a conflict, to inflamed skin, and finally to flaring desire.
sensesIntro.cn: inflame 从「点燃某物」出发，引申到激起情绪、使冲突恶化、皮肤发炎，最后指燃起欲望。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flame that jumps from a spark and grows quickly.
core.cn: 核心意象：一小簇火从火星里窜出，迅速变大。

branches.en: Setting something burning is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 使某物燃烧是最字面的义项。

branches.en: A fire inside a person becomes excited feeling.
branches.cn: 火烧到人心里，就成了被激起的情绪。

branches.en: A fed fire that will not be put out makes a bad situation worse.
branches.cn: 只添柴不扑灭的火，正对应让糟糕局势更糟。

branches.en: The heat of burning skin is the old medical picture of inflammation.
branches.cn: 皮肤发热红肿呼应古代医学对炎症的「内在之火」想象。

branches.en: Emotion and desire are two temperatures of the same inner fire.
branches.cn: 情绪与欲望是同一团内心之火的两个温度。

intro.en: Inflame pairs the Latin prefix in- with the flame root, and the family includes inflammation, inflammatory, and flammable.
intro.cn: inflame 把拉丁语前缀 in- 与「火焰」词根组合起来，同族词包括 inflammation、inflammatory 与 flammable。

latinIntro.en: Latin flamma means flame, and inflammare means to set on fire or to excite.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 flamma 意为火焰，inflammare 意为点燃或激起。

items.example: The prefix in- adds a sense of causing.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 增添「使之」的意思。

items.example: Flamma gives the fire image.
items.exampleCN: flamma 提供火的意象。

items.example: Inflammare is the direct source of the verb.
items.exampleCN: inflammare 是这个动词的直接来源。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或状态的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ation forms inflammation.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成 inflammation。

items.meaningCN: 表示「引起……的」的形容词后缀
items.example: The suffix -atory forms inflammatory.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -atory 构成 inflammatory。

items.example: The suffix -able forms inflammable.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 构成 inflammable。

items.meaning: fire burning in a bright tongue
items.example: Flame keeps the root meaning in plain English.
items.exampleCN: flame 在普通英语中保留词根含义。

items.example: Inflammation is the medical form of the word.
items.exampleCN: inflammation 是该词的医学形式。

items.example: Inflammatory describes words that stir people up.
items.exampleCN: inflammatory 描述能激起人们的言辞。

definition_zh: 易燃的，易着火的；易怒的，容易被激怒的；含感情的，热烈的
definition_en: easily set on fire; also, easily stirred to anger or strong feeling
core_image: 一根火柴靠近，东西「呼」地一下烧起来：一点就着
scene: 加油站里，工作人员提醒司机不要把油桶放在太阳底下。Fuel is inflammable, so do not leave the cans in direct sunlight.
sceneCN: 这里 inflammable 是「易燃的」（第 1 个义项：一点火就会燃烧）；句意：燃料易燃，所以不要把油罐留在太阳直射的地方。

derivatives.zh: 易燃性；易怒的性格
易燃地
非易燃的；不如 non-flammable 常用

senses.title: Easily set on fire
senses.definition: able to catch fire and burn quickly
senses.definitionCN: 能够很快着火并升腾燃烧的
senses.example: Paint thinners are highly inflammable liquids.
senses.exampleCN: 稀释剂是极易燃的液体。
senses.why: The Latin root flamma means flame, and the prefix in- here is intensive, so the image is something that flames up at once.
senses.whyCN: 词根 flamma 是「火焰」，此前缀表示加强，因此画面是一碰火就猛地燃起来。

senses.title: Easily stirred to anger
senses.definition: quick to become angry or excited
senses.definitionCN: 很容易生气或激动的
senses.example: He has an inflammable temper that frightens the staff.
senses.exampleCN: 他脾气火爆，让员工们害怕。
senses.why: From flames the word extends to feelings: anger that flares up as fast as a fire catching.
senses.whyCN: 由火焰引申到情绪：怒火像物体着火一样，一触就腾起来。

senses.title: Likely to cause strong feeling
senses.definition: likely to cause strong emotion, argument, or angry reaction
senses.definitionCN: 容易引发强烈情绪、争论或愤怒反应的
senses.example: Religion can be an inflammable subject at dinner parties.
senses.exampleCN: 在晚宴上，宗教是个容易引发争论的话题。
senses.why: Any topic that makes people blaze with argument is pictured as fuel ready to catch light.
senses.whyCN: 凡能让人争论得面红耳赤的话题，都被想成一点就着的燃料。

intro.en: Inflammable comes from Latin inflammare, to set on fire, built from in- plus flamma, a flame.
intro.cn: inflammable 来自拉丁语 inflammare（点着、使燃烧），由 in- 加 flamma（火焰）构成。

items.en: Flamma means a flame or blaze.
items.cn: flamma 意为火焰、火光。

items.en: Inflammare means to set on fire or kindle.
items.cn: inflammare 意为点燃、使燃烧。

items.en: Inflammabilis means able to be set on fire.
items.cn: inflammabilis 意为可被点燃的。

items.en: Inflammable passes through French into English.
items.cn: inflammable 经由法语进入英语。

items.en: The sense of a fiery temper develops from the fire image.
items.cn: 到了十七世纪前后，由火焰意象发展出「火爆脾气」的含义。

items.en: Safety labels often prefer flammable or non-flammable, because in- can wrongly suggest not.
items.cn: 现代安全标识常改用 flammable 或 non-flammable，因为前缀 in- 容易被误读为「不」。

note.en: Inflammable shares its flame root with flame and inflame, and shares meaning with combustible and fiery.
note.cn: inflammable 与 flame 一族的词形相近，意义上与「可燃的、火热的」一组词相邻。

entries.definition: burning gas that gives light and heat
to cause to burn or to become angry
easily set on fire, the modern safety term
entries.definitionCN: 易燃的；现代安全标识里与 inflammable 同义的替代说法

entries.definition: able to catch fire and burn
easily angered and passionate
evaporating quickly or changing mood suddenly

normalIntro.en: Inflammable carries the Latin flame root flamma, so the word itself holds the picture of fire.
normalIntro.cn: inflammable 里藏着拉丁语的火焰词根 flamma，整个词就是一簇火苗。

normal.en: Look inside the word and find flame: inflammable means full of flame.
normal.cn: 往词里看，能找到 flame：inflammable 就是「充满火」的。

normal.en: An inflam-mat is a mat that bursts into flames at a touch.
normal.cn: 把词拆成 in 加 flam 加 mable，就像一张一碰就起火的垫子。

normal.en: The prefix in- here intensifies rather than negates, so the verb inflame means to set something burning.
normal.cn: 这里的前缀是加强语气而不是否定，所以动词 inflame 是把东西点着。

normal.en: Remember the safety pairing: flammable and non-flammable are the plain labels used on tanks today.
normal.cn: 记住安全标识的搭配：现代油罐上多用 flammable 与 non-flammable 这组直白标签。

normal.en: Compare inflation: both come from flamma, one is money warming up, the other is fuel catching fire.
normal.cn: 对比 inflation：两者都源于 flamma，一个是钱在升温，一个是燃料着火。

abstract.en: Picture a single spark landing on a pile of dry straw.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗火星落在干草堆上。

abstract.en: See a man whose face reddens the moment someone disagrees.
abstract.cn: 想象一个被人反驳就立刻满脸通红的人。

abstract.en: Think of a dinner party where one word sets the whole table into argument.
abstract.cn: 想象晚宴上只因一句话，全桌人立刻吵成一团。

examples.en: Workers must store inflammable chemicals in a cool, locked cupboard.
examples.cn: 工人必须把易燃化学品存放在阴凉上锁的柜子里。

examples.en: His inflammable temper made every meeting tense.
examples.cn: 他火爆的脾气让每次会议都很紧张。

examples.en: The old label read inflammable, and the new one reads flammable, but the danger is the same.
examples.cn: 旧标签写 inflammable，新标签写 flammable，但危险是一样的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因弗拉姆博」—— 因弗拉姆博士一碰就「燃」，一点就着的脾气；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 flamma（火焰）→ inflammare（点燃）→ 拉丁语 inflammabilis（可被点燃的）→ 古法语 → 英语 inflammable；核心义「一碰就燃」。

sensesIntro.en: Inflammable moves from physical fire that catches at once, to a temper that flares, and finally to topics that set people arguing.
sensesIntro.cn: inflammable 从「一碰就着的火」出发，先指易燃的物体，再指火爆的脾气，最后指容易点燃争论的话题。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a piece of cloth that catches fire the instant a flame touches it.
core.cn: 核心意象：布片一碰到火苗就立刻烧起来。

branches.en: Physical fuel that burns at once is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 一点就燃的实物材料是本义。

branches.en: A person whose anger flares up keeps the fire image for temper.
branches.cn: 脾气一触就起的人，把火焰意象留给了情绪。

branches.en: A topic that causes argument is fuel for angry feelings.
branches.cn: 容易引发争论的话题，就是引爆愤怒情绪的燃料。

branches.en: Both senses rely on heat that spreads fast once started.
branches.cn: 两个义项都依赖「一旦开始就迅速蔓延的热」。

branches.en: An inflammable temper and an inflammable topic often appear together in an argument.
branches.cn: 火爆的脾气和易起争议的话题常常在争吵中同时出现。

intro.en: Inflammable is a two-layer word: an intensive prefix in-, the Latin root flamm-, and the suffix -able for being able to be acted on.
intro.cn: inflammable 是三层结构：加强前缀 in-、拉丁词根 flamm-（火）、词尾 -able（能够被……的）。

latinIntro.en: Latin flamma means flame, and the verb flammare means to burn or set alight.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 flamma 意为火焰，动词 flammare 意为燃烧或点燃。

items.example: Flamma gives the whole flame family.
items.exampleCN: flamma 提供了整个火焰词族。

items.example: Flammare leads to inflammare.
items.exampleCN: flammare 演变出 inflammare。

items.example: The prefix in- strengthens the verb to mean set on fire.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 加强语气，使动词意为「点着火」。

items.example: Inflammabilis means capable of burning.
items.exampleCN: inflammabilis 意为可被点燃的。

items.example: The suffix -able shapes the English word.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成英语词形。

items.example: The suffix -ity builds inflammability.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 inflammability。

items.meaning: to set on fire or to anger
items.example: Inflame drops the suffix.
items.exampleCN: inflame 去掉了抽象词尾。

items.example: Non- joins flammable in safety labels.
items.exampleCN: non- 与 flammable 组合，用于安全标识。

items.example: Inflammability names the property.
items.exampleCN: inflammability 指这种性质。

latinEntries.meaning: able to be set on fire

definition_zh: 可充气的，可膨胀的；（可充气的）充气制品，如充气船、充气床垫
definition_en: able to be filled with air so that it becomes firm and larger; also a rubber or plastic object of this kind
core_image: 一个软塌塌的橡胶圈，被气筒一点点吹鼓起来
scene: 暑假去海边，行李里塞了一只扁扁的橡皮艇。We packed an inflatable boat for the beach holiday.
sceneCN: 这里 inflatable 是「充气的」（第 1 个义项：可以被充气而鼓起来的）；句意：我们为海边度假装了一只充气船。

pos.zh: 充气制品；充气船（常用复数 inflatables）

derivatives.zh: 给……充气过头（in- 换为 over- 构成的同族词）
充气；通货膨胀（同为 inflate 加名词词尾）
可放气的（以 de- 反前缀构成）

senses.title: Able to be filled with air
senses.definition: designed to be filled with air or gas so that it swells and becomes firm
senses.definitionCN: 设计成可以充入空气或气体，从而鼓胀并变硬的
senses.example: The children slept on an inflatable mattress in the tent.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们睡在帐篷里的充气床垫上。
senses.why: In- brings air inward, flare means to blow, and -able marks what can be blown up, so the word names a thing designed to swell.
senses.whyCN: 词缀 in- 表示向内，flare 意为吹气，-able 表示「可以被……」，因此这个词指为鼓胀而造的东西。

senses.title: A rubber or plastic object of this kind
senses.definition: a rubber or plastic object that must be filled with air before use
senses.definitionCN: 必须充气后才能使用的橡胶或塑料制品
senses.example: Coastguards rescued the family in a bright orange inflatable.
senses.exampleCN: 海岸警卫队用一艘亮橙色的充气船救起了这家人。
senses.why: The adjective turns into a noun because people need a short name for the boat, raft, or toy itself.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转为名词，因为人们需要一个简短名称来指船、筏或玩具本身。

senses.title: An inflatable structure for play or shows
senses.titleCN: 充气城堡一类的充气设施
senses.definition: a large air-filled structure such as a bouncy castle, often used at fairs and parties
senses.definitionCN: 充气城堡一类的大型充气结构，常用于集市和派对
senses.example: The fair rented three inflatables for the children.
senses.exampleCN: 集市为孩子们租了三套充气设施。
senses.why: The same core notion of blowing the object up creates a bigger, party-sized version of it.
senses.whyCN: 同样是「把东西吹鼓」这一核心概念，只是造出了派对规模的放大版。

intro.en: Inflatable is a modern English word made from the verb inflate, which comes from Latin inflare, to blow into.
intro.cn: inflatable 是现代英语用动词 inflate 加词尾造出来的词，而 inflate 来自拉丁语 inflare（吹进去）。

items.en: Flare means to blow or breathe.
items.cn: flare 意为吹、呼气。

items.en: Inflare means to blow into or puff up.
items.cn: inflare 意为往里面吹，使鼓起。

items.en: Inflatus means blown up, puffed out, or swollen.
items.cn: inflatus 意为被吹起的、鼓胀的。

items.en: The verb inflate records the meaning to blow in or swell up.
items.cn: 动词 inflate 在十五世纪出现，意为吹入、膨胀。

items.en: Rubber and later plastic manufacture give the adjective inflatable a practical home.
items.cn: 橡胶乃至后来的塑料制造，让形容词 inflatable 有了实际用武之地。

items.en: Inflatable is used as a noun for boats, mattresses, and bouncy castles.
items.cn: 现代英语里 inflatable 可作名词，指充气船、充气床垫与充气城堡。

note.en: Inflatable sits in the inflate word family, and in meaning it is close to blow-up and pneumatic objects.
note.cn: inflatable 属于 inflate 一族，意义上与「吹起的、风动的」物品相邻。

entries.definition: to fill something with air so that it swells
the act of filling with air, or a general rise in prices
to let air out of something
filled with air and made larger
worked or filled by air or gas
entries.definitionCN: 由空气或气体驱动的；气压式的

entries.definition: able to float or keep something afloat

normalIntro.en: Inflatable is built from the verb inflate plus the suffix -able, so it describes anything that air can blow up.
normalIntro.cn: inflatable 由动词 inflate 加词尾 -able 构成，所以它描述的是任何能被空气吹鼓的东西。

normal.en: Split it as inflate plus able: able to be inflated.
normal.cn: 拆成 inflate 加 able：能够被充气的。

normal.en: The safety labels on aircraft announce an inflatable life vest under every seat.
normal.cn: 飞机上的安全标识会提到每个座位下都有充气救生衣。

normal.en: Inflate comes from a Latin word meaning to blow in, and the prefix in- carries the direction inward.
normal.cn: inflate 来自拉丁语「往里面吹」，而前缀 in 正表示「向内」。

normal.en: Compare the pair: deflate lets air out, inflate pushes air in, so inflatable names the bag that fills.
normal.cn: 对比一对：deflate 放气，inflate 打气，那么 inflatable 就是那个被充满的袋子。

normal.en: As a noun it often takes an -s: inflatables means all the boats and castles together.
normal.cn: 作名词时常加 -s：inflatables 统指各种充气船和充气城堡。

abstract.en: Watch a beach ball flicker from a flat sheet into a round globe with every pump.
abstract.cn: 想象一只沙滩球随着每次打气，从扁平的皮片鼓成圆球。

abstract.en: See a bright orange rubber boat bouncing on the waves like a toy.
abstract.cn: 想象一只橙色橡皮船像玩具一样在浪上颠动。

abstract.en: Picture a bouncy castle rising within minutes from a folded heap on the grass.
abstract.cn: 想象草地上的一堆折叠物在几分钟内立成一座充气城堡。

examples.en: They paddled the inflatable across the lake at sunset.
examples.cn: 他们在日落时划着充气艇过湖。

examples.en: Inflatable seats make the hall easy to rearrange.
examples.cn: 充气座椅让礼堂布置起来很方便。

examples.en: The shop sells ropes, jackets, and inflatables for the summer season.
examples.cn: 这家店夏季出售绳索、救生衣和各种充气用品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因弗莱特波」—— 念作「因弗莱特伯」，想象一个叫弗莱特的人把管子凑到嘴边「波」地一吹，船就鼓了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 flare（吹）→ in-（向内）+ flare = inflare（吹进去）→ 英语 inflate（充气、膨胀）→ inflate + -able → inflatable「可被充气的」；核心义「往里吹气使它鼓起来」。

sensesIntro.en: Inflatable begins as an adjective for things that can be blown up with air, then turns into a noun for the boats and toys themselves, and later for big party structures.
sensesIntro.cn: inflatable 先作形容词，指能用空气吹鼓的东西；再转为名词，指充气船和玩具本身；后来还指大型充气游乐设施。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rubber ring that swells as the pump fills it with air.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个橡皮圈随着打气筒注入空气而渐渐鼓起。

branches.en: The adjective names anything that is designed to be filled with air.
branches.cn: 形容词义指任何为充气而设计的东西。

branches.en: The noun names the boat, mattress, or raft itself.
branches.cn: 名词义指充气船、床垫或筏子本身。

branches.en: Big play structures reuse the noun for large party-sized objects.
branches.cn: 大型游乐设施把名词义用于派对规模的大物件。

branches.en: The adjective and the noun share the same air-filled object: a flat sheet that must be blown up before use.
branches.cn: 形容词义与名词义共享同一个充气物：一张使用前必须吹鼓的扁皮。

branches.en: Both nouns emphasise the moment of being filled on site, then packed away flat.
branches.cn: 两个名词义都强调现场充气、之后再放气收平的这一面。

intro.en: Inflatable joins the prefix in-, the Latin root flat- from flare, and the English suffix -able.
intro.cn: inflatable 由前缀 in-、源自 flare 的拉丁词根 flat- 和英语词尾 -able 拼成。

latinIntro.en: Latin flare means to blow, and inflare means to blow into something.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 flare 意为吹，inflare 意为往某物里面吹。

items.example: Flare gives the breath image.
items.exampleCN: flare 提供「吹气」的意象。

items.example: The prefix in- turns blowing into blowing in.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 把「吹」变成「往里吹」。

items.example: Inflatus means blown into.
items.exampleCN: inflatus 意为被吹入的。

items.meaningCN: 由拉丁词形构成动词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ate shapes the verb inflate.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 构成动词 inflate。

items.example: The suffix -able forms inflatable.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成 inflatable。

items.meaningCN: 向下；离开（这里引申为放掉）
items.example: De- gives the opposite verb deflate.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 de- 构成反义动词 deflate。

items.example: Inflatable plus the plural -s becomes a noun.
items.exampleCN: inflatable 加复数词尾后作名词。

items.example: The suffix -tion forms inflation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -tion 构成 inflation。

items.meaning: the act of inflating, or rising prices
items.example: Inflation keeps the air image for money.
items.exampleCN: inflation 把充气意象用到货币上。

definition_zh: 给……充气，使膨胀；使膨胀（数量、价格、规模）；夸大，吹嘘；膨胀（指物价、经济）；使骄傲自满
definition_en: to fill something with air or gas so that it swells; to make an amount or price rise or seem larger than it is; to become puffed up with pride
core_image: 一只气球被不断往里打气，越鼓越大，直到表皮绷紧
scene: 新闻报道说，几家公司为了骗取补贴，故意把报表上的数字做大。Some firms inflated their sales figures to win more subsidies.
sceneCN: 这里 inflate 是「虚报、抬高（数字）」（第 2 个义项：把数量说得比实际大）；句意：一些公司虚报销售额，以求拿到更多补贴。

collocations.zh: 使货币膨胀（发行过多货币）

derivatives.zh: 充气；通货膨胀（inflate + -ion）
充了气的；被夸大的（inflate + -ed）
可充气的（inflate + -able）
充气泵；充气装置（inflate + -or）
给……放气；使泄气（de- 反前缀）
（经济）再膨胀；用增加货币刺激经济

senses.title: To fill with air or gas
senses.definition: to put air or gas into something so that it becomes firm and larger
senses.definitionCN: 往某物里注入空气或气体，使它变硬、变大
senses.example: She inflated the bicycle tyres before the long ride.
senses.exampleCN: 长途骑行前，她给自行车轮胎打了气。
senses.why: The Latin verb inflare means to blow into, so the first sense is simply air blown inward until the object swells.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 inflare 意为「往里面吹」，所以第一个义项就是空气被吹进去、物体随之鼓胀。

senses.title: To make a number or price seem larger
senses.definition: to make an amount, price, or claim larger than it really is
senses.definitionCN: 把数量、价格或说法说得比实际更大
senses.example: The dealer inflated the value of the old car.
senses.exampleCN: 经销商抬高了这辆旧车的估价。
senses.why: A number can be puffed up like a balloon: the figure looks fatter without more substance behind it.
senses.whyCN: 数字也能像气球一样被吹鼓：看起来更大，背后却没有更多实质内容。

senses.title: To increase beyond the real level
senses.definition: to cause prices, currency, or an economy to grow beyond their real value
senses.definitionCN: 使物价、货币或经济膨胀到超过真实水平
senses.example: Too much cheap credit can inflate house prices.
senses.exampleCN: 过多的廉价信贷会抬高房价。
senses.why: Money itself is seen as air in the economic balloon, and adding too much makes the whole thing swell.
senses.whyCN: 在经济这个气球里，钱被当作空气，注入过多，整个东西就胀起来。

senses.title: To become proud and self-important
senses.definition: to become puffed up with pride or a sense of importance
senses.definitionCN: 因骄傲或自视甚高而变得飘起来
senses.example: Praise from the coach began to inflate his opinion of himself.
senses.exampleCN: 教练的夸奖让他越来越自我膨胀。
senses.why: Pride is pictured as air inside a person: the more it is pumped in, the lighter and more puffed up one feels.
senses.whyCN: 骄傲被想象成人肚里的空气：气打进去越多，人就越轻、越膨胀。

intro.en: Inflate goes back to Latin inflare, made of in- meaning in, plus flare meaning to blow.
intro.cn: inflate 可追溯到拉丁语 inflare，由 in-（进入）加 flare（吹）构成。

items.en: The reconstructed root bhel- is often linked to swelling and blowing.
items.cn: 一般认为重构词根 bhel- 与「膨胀、吹」有关（重构形式）。

items.en: Flare means to blow or breathe out, and inflare means to blow into.
items.cn: flare 意为吹、呼气，inflare 意为往里面吹。

items.en: Inflatus is the participle, blown up or puffed out.
items.cn: inflatus 是分词形式，意为被吹起的、鼓胀的。

items.en: Inflate enters English from Latin inflatus with the sense to swell or puff up.
items.cn: inflate 在十五世纪前后经拉丁语 inflatus 进入英语，义为膨胀、吹鼓。

items.en: By the 1600s the word is used for blowing up beliefs, hopes, and prices.
items.cn: 到了十七世纪，它被用来表示把信心、希望、价格吹大。

items.en: Economics gives the derived inflation its dominant modern sense.
items.cn: 经济学让派生词 inflation 获得了现代最主要的含义。

note.en: Inflate belongs to the flat word family of blow words, and stands beside swell, exaggerate, and deflate.
note.cn: inflate 属于以「吹」为根的词族，并与 swell、exaggerate、deflate 这些词相邻。

entries.definition: the act of filling with air, or a rise in prices
to let air out of something
able to be filled with air
to become larger and rounder
to make something seem bigger than it is
to swell with air or with pride

normalIntro.en: Inflate is a single image of a pump: air goes in, and whatever it touches puffs out.
normalIntro.cn: inflate 就是一个打气筒的画面：空气进去，被吹到的东西就鼓起来。

normal.en: Keep the Latin pair in mind: in- means into and flare means to blow.
normal.cn: 记住这对拉丁词：in- 表示「向内」，flare 表示「吹」。

normal.en: Inflate and deflate are a matched pair, one pumps air in, the other lets it out.
normal.cn: inflate 与 deflate 是配对的一对：一个往里打气，一个把气放掉。

normal.en: The noun inflation grew from the same root and now names rising prices.
normal.cn: 名词 inflation 出自同一词根，如今主要表示物价上涨。

normal.en: In news reports, the verb inflate is often followed by figures, prices, or profits.
normal.cn: 新闻报道里，这个动词后面常跟 figures、prices、profits 这类词。

normal.en: Add -ed to get inflated, the adjective behind inflated prices and inflated egos.
normal.cn: 加上 -ed 得到形容词 inflated，常用于 inflated prices 与 inflated egos。

abstract.en: See a balloon growing with each stroke of the pump until the skin is tight.
abstract.cn: 想象气球随着每一下打气越鼓越大，表皮绷得发紧。

abstract.en: Watch a sales chart redrawn higher and higher with a thick marker.
abstract.cn: 想象有人用粗笔把销售曲线一次比一次画得更高。

abstract.en: Picture a city where every price tag is replaced with a bigger one overnight.
abstract.cn: 想象一座城市里，一夜之间每张价签都换成了数字更大的。

examples.en: Airbags inflate in a fraction of a second during a crash.
examples.cn: 发生碰撞时，安全气囊会在零点几秒内充气。

examples.en: Retailers are accused of inflating prices before the sale.
examples.cn: 零售商被指在促销前故意抬高价格。

examples.en: His ego was inflated by years of constant praise.
examples.cn: 多年不断的赞美让他自我膨胀。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因弗莱特」—— 想象一台打气筒名叫「弗莱特」，一按按钮「弗」地往里灌气，气球就鼓了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 flare（吹）→ in-（向内）+ flare = inflare（往里吹）→ 拉丁语 inflatus（鼓起的）→ 英语 inflate；核心义「往里面吹气，使它鼓起来」。

sensesIntro.en: Inflate starts with air blown into a physical object, then the image moves to money and numbers that are blown up, and finally to a person puffed up with pride.
sensesIntro.cn: inflate 从往实物里吹气开始，接着把「吹大」用在数字和金钱上，最后用在因骄傲而膨胀的人身上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balloon swelling tight as the pump blows air into it.
core.cn: 核心意象：打气筒把空气吹进去，气球鼓得绷紧。

branches.en: The literal sense is air going into a tyre, balloon, or mattress.
branches.cn: 本义是空气进入轮胎、气球或床垫。

branches.en: Numbers and prices are treated as things that can be blown larger.
branches.cn: 数字和价格被当成可以吹大的东西。

branches.en: The economy and prices swell because too much money is like too much air.
branches.cn: 经济与物价膨胀，因为过多的钱就像过多的空气。

branches.en: Pride is air inside a person, and being praised pumps it in.
branches.cn: 骄傲是人肚子里的空气，而被夸奖就是在往里打气。

branches.en: Inflated figures and inflated prices both feed the wider income of inflation.
branches.cn: 虚报的数字与被抬高的价格，都汇入通货膨胀这个大概念。

intro.en: Inflate is a Latin participle turned English verb: the prefix in-, the root flat- from flare, and the verb ending -ate.
intro.cn: inflate 是拉丁语分词转成的英语动词：前缀 in-、源自 flare 的词根 flat- 和动词词尾 -ate。

latinIntro.en: Latin flare means to blow, and inflare means to blow air into something.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 flare 意为吹，inflare 意为把空气吹进某物。

items.example: Flare gives the blowing image.
items.exampleCN: flare 提供「吹气」的意象。

items.example: The prefix in- directs the air inward.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 把气流引向内部。

items.example: Inflare is the direct source of inflate.
items.exampleCN: inflare 是 inflate 的直接来源。

items.example: Inflatus supplies the participle base.
items.exampleCN: inflatus 提供分词词干。

items.example: The suffix -ate gives the English verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 使英语动词成形。

items.example: De- reverses the action in deflate.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 de- 在 deflate 中反转动作。

items.example: The suffix -ion forms inflation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 构成 inflation。

items.example: The suffix -able forms inflatable.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成 inflatable。

items.meaning: a person or device that does
items.example: The suffix -or forms inflator.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -or 构成 inflator。

items.example: Re- gives the economic verb reflate.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 构成经济用语 reflate。

definition_zh: 使遭受（痛苦、伤害、惩罚）；把（不快之事）强加于；予以打击
definition_en: to make someone suffer something unpleasant, such as pain, damage, or punishment
core_image: 一只手按下印章，痛苦像印记一样被硬盖在对方身上
scene: 军队撤离后，这座小镇的居民仍在承受战争留下的伤痛。The war left deep wounds that the townspeople still inflict on themselves in memory.
sceneCN: 这里 inflict 是「施加伤害」（第 1 个义项：使某人遭受痛苦或损害）；句意：战争留下深深的伤口，镇上的人至今仍在回忆中给自己施加这种伤痛。

pos.zh: 使遭受；使承受（痛苦、伤害、惩罚）
强加；施加（不受欢迎的事物）

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀 -tion 构成，义为「施加；使遭受（痛苦）」
由动词加 -er 构成，指「施加痛苦或惩罚的人」
由 self-（自身）与过去分词复合构成，义为「自己造成的」
由动词加形容词后缀 -ive 构成，义为「施加性的；造成痛苦的」

senses.title: To make someone suffer pain or damage
senses.definition: to cause a person or thing to experience pain, damage, or loss
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或某物经历痛苦、损害或损失
senses.example: The storm inflicted heavy damage on the coastal village.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨给沿海村庄造成了严重损害。
senses.why: The Latin prefix in- means on, and the root means struck, so inflicting is striking something onto a target.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语前缀 in- 意为「在……之上」，词根意为「打击」，所以 inflict 就是把打击落到目标身上，痛苦被硬塞给对方。

senses.title: To impose something unwelcome on someone
senses.definition: to force an unwanted thing, such as advice or company, on another person
senses.definitionCN: 把他人不想要的东西（如建议、陪伴）强加给对方
senses.example: He inflicted his opinions on everyone at dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 晚饭时他把自己的看法强加给在座的每一个人。
senses.why: If a blow can be delivered onto someone, so can anything unpleasant or tiresome, and the image keeps its force.
senses.whyCN: 既然打击可以被送到对方身上，任何令人不快或厌烦的东西也可以被送过去，意象中的「强加力量」保留了下来。

senses.title: To impose a punishment or penalty
senses.definition: to give someone a punishment, penalty, or legal sanction
senses.definitionCN: 给予某人惩罚、处罚或法律制裁
senses.example: The court inflicted a heavy fine on the firm.
senses.exampleCN: 法院对这家公司处以高额罚款。
senses.why: Punishment is the most formal kind of pain that is deliberately placed on a person by an authority.
senses.whyCN: 惩罚是权威有意加诸某人身上的最正式的痛苦，正好延续「把痛苦硬按下去」的核心画面。

senses.title: To cause wounds of war or violence
senses.titleCN: 造成（战争或暴力的）伤亡
senses.definition: to cause casualties, wounds, or losses in fighting or in a violent event
senses.definitionCN: 在战斗或暴力事件中造成伤亡、创伤或损失
senses.example: The attackers inflicted heavy casualties on the defence.
senses.exampleCN: 进攻方给守军造成了重大伤亡。
senses.why: The Old French verbs for striking and defeating brought the military image straight into English.
senses.whyCN: 古法语中表示「打击」和「击败」的动词把军事画面直接带入英语，所以 inflict 常用于描述战场上的杀伤。

senses.title: To cause damage to a thing
senses.definition: to do harm to an object, building, or natural system
senses.definitionCN: 对物体、建筑或自然系统造成破坏
senses.example: The insects inflicted serious damage on the crops.
senses.exampleCN: 这些昆虫对庄稼造成了严重破坏。
senses.why: The patient of the verb need not be a person, so damage done to things keeps the same striking image.
senses.whyCN: 动词的承受者不必是人，落在事物上的破坏也沿用同一种「打击落下」的画面。

senses.title: To cause emotional hurt
senses.definition: to cause someone emotional distress or embarrassment
senses.definitionCN: 给某人造成情绪上的痛苦或难堪
senses.example: His careless words inflicted real hurt on her.
senses.exampleCN: 他随口的话给她造成了真正的伤害。
senses.why: Physical wounds became emotional ones, and the sense of a blow landed on a person did not change.
senses.whyCN: 身体的伤口延伸为情绪上的伤口，而「一下打在某人身上」的感受并没有改变。

senses.title: To strike or land a blow
senses.definition: to deliver a blow or a strike, especially in older or literary use
senses.definitionCN: 予以一击或打击，多见于较早或文学语境
senses.example: The knight inflicted a blow upon the shield.
senses.exampleCN: 骑士在盾牌上重重一击。
senses.why: The oldest layer of the word is simply to strike, before the striking came to be seen as producing suffering.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早的层次就是「打击」，后来才把打击理解为产生痛苦的来源，所以最具体的「击打」义仍然保留。

senses.title: To impose a burden or cost
senses.definition: to place a burden, cost, or difficulty on people or institutions
senses.definitionCN: 使人们或机构承担负担、代价或困难
senses.example: The new tax inflicted a heavy burden on small shops.
senses.exampleCN: 新税给小店铺带来了沉重负担。
senses.why: From punishment and damage it is a short step to abstract burdens imposed by rules and policies.
senses.whyCN: 从惩罚和损害再往前走一步，就是规则与政策加在人们身上的抽象负担，这条义项由此长出。

intro.en: Inflict comes through Old French from Latin infligere, to strike against or impose, built on in-, meaning on, and fligere, to strike.
intro.cn: inflict 经由古法语来自拉丁语 infligere（打击、施加），由 in-（在……之上）与 fligere（打击）构成。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning to strike, which also underlies Latin and Greek descriptions of blows.
items.cn: 一般认为有表示「打击」的原始印欧语词根（重构形式），拉丁语与希腊语中的击打类词都与它有关。

items.en: Fligere means to strike, and the prefixed verb infligere means to strike against or bring upon.
items.cn: fligere 意为「打击」，加上前缀的 infligere 意为「打击于」或「加于」。

items.en: Infligere develops the legal and moral sense of imposing a penalty on someone.
items.cn: infligere 进一步发展出法律与道德意义上「施加刑罚」的用法。

items.en: The Old French verbs reflecting this shape settle the word into the form that English later borrowed.
items.cn: 古法语中表述这一形态的动词固定下来，成为英语后来借入的形式基础。

items.en: Inflict enters English in the late medieval period, first as a learned verb for striking and for giving punishment.
items.cn: inflict 在中古英语后期进入英语，最初是书面语中的动词，用于「打击」和「施加刑罚」。

items.en: Modern English extends the verb to damage, casualties, costs, and emotional harm.
items.cn: 现代英语把它的用法扩展到损害、伤亡、代价和情感伤害。

note.en: Inflict is the verb of landing pain on someone, close in form to inflict-related words and near in meaning to impose and cause.
note.cn: inflict 是把痛苦「打」到别人身上的动词，形式上与同族词相邻，意义上与「强加」「造成」类词相邻。

normalIntro.en: Inflict is a strike brought onto someone: the prefix in- means on, and the old root means to strike.
normalIntro.cn: inflict 是打到别人身上的一击：前缀 in- 表示「在上」，古老词根表示「打击」。

normal.en: The fixed pattern is inflict something on someone, just as pain is placed onto a target.
normal.cn: 固定搭配是 inflict something on someone，就像把痛苦放到目标身上。

normal.en: Inflict collocates strongly with damage, pain, casualties, and punishment.
normal.cn: inflict 常与 damage、pain、casualties、punishment 等词搭配。

normal.en: Keep infliction and inflict together: the noun names the act, the verb names the doing.
normal.cn: 把 infliction 与 inflict 放在一起记：名词指施加这一行为，动词指施加这个动作。

normal.en: Compare afflict: afflict troubles its subject from inside, inflict delivers harm to an object.
normal.cn: 对比 afflict：afflict 让主语自身受苦，inflict 是把伤害送到对象身上。

normal.en: Self-inflicted and inflictive belong to the same family and keep the sense of harm brought on someone.
normal.cn: self-inflicted 与 inflictive 同属这个家族，都保留「把伤害施加出去」的含义。

abstract.en: Picture a heavy seal pressed onto paper, and the pain is cut into the surface.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚沉重的印章压在纸上，痛苦被硬压进表面。

abstract.en: Imagine handing someone a package they never asked for and will not want.
abstract.cn: 想象把一件对方从未索要、也不会想要的包裹硬塞给他。

abstract.en: Think of a judge slamming the penalty stamp down on a desk.
abstract.cn: 想象法官把处罚印章重重盖在桌上。

examples.en: The rebels inflicted heavy losses on the occupying army.
examples.cn: 叛军给占领军造成了重大损失。

examples.en: Drought can inflict lasting damage on fragile farmland.
examples.cn: 干旱会给脆弱的农田造成持久的损害。

examples.en: Try not to inflict your worries on your friends all the time.
examples.cn: 尽量不要总把自己的担忧强加给朋友。

root: 拉丁语 fligere（打击）+ 前缀 in-（在……之上）→ infligere（打击、加于）→ 古法语 → 英语 inflict，核心义「把打击落到某人身上」。

sensesIntro.en: Inflict starts with the concrete blow of damage and wounds, moves to emotional pain, then to imposed and unwelcome burdens such as punishment and cost.
sensesIntro.cn: inflict 从具体的打击开始——损害、伤亡、身体伤口，再过渡到情感伤害，最后抽象为惩罚、负担与代价等被强加于人的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressing a blow down onto someone who cannot refuse it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把打击硬按到无法拒绝的对方身上。

branches.en: Physical and material harm both leave a visible mark of the strike.
branches.cn: 身体伤害与物质损害都会留下打击的可见痕迹。

branches.en: The unwelcome thing is pressed on someone the way an imposition is.
branches.cn: 不受欢迎的东西像硬塞的负担一样被按到别人身上。

branches.en: Punishment is a formal blow delivered by authority.
branches.cn: 惩罚是权威正式挥下的一击。

branches.en: The battlefield keeps the oldest literal sense of landing a blow.
branches.cn: 战场仍保留最古老的字面含义：一击落到实处。

branches.en: Some wounds are emotional and leave no mark on the body.
branches.cn: 有些伤口是情感上的，身体上看不见痕迹。

intro.en: Inflict is built from the Latin prefix in- plus the striking root fligere, with the noun infliction and several English compounds around it.
intro.cn: inflict 由拉丁语前缀 in- 与表示「打击」的词根 fligere 构成，周围有名词 infliction 以及若干英语复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin fligere means to strike, and the prefixed verb infligere means to strike against or bring upon.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fligere 意为「打击」，带前缀的 infligere 意为「打击于」或「加于」。

items.example: The prefix in- in infligere places the blow on a target.
items.exampleCN: inflict 中的前缀 in- 把打击放到目标之上。

items.example: Fligere supplies the striking image at the heart of the word.
items.exampleCN: fligere 提供了这个词核心的「打击」意象。

items.example: Infligere already pairs a blow with a penalty.
items.exampleCN: infligere 已经把「打击」和「刑罚」结合在一起。

definition_zh: 施加（痛苦、惩罚）；痛苦之事；折磨；被施加的处罚
definition_en: the act of causing pain, suffering, or punishment to someone, or the pain that is caused
core_image: 一只按着印章的手终于抬起，纸面上留下压下去的痛苦印记
scene: 冬天夜里，一家人围着火炉回忆当年战乱给他们带来的苦楚。Years later, the family still spoke of the infliction of those winters with a shiver.
sceneCN: 这里 infliction 是「施加、使遭受」（第 1 个义项：把痛苦施加于人的行为）；句意：多年以后，一家人提起那几个冬天所受的痛苦，仍会打个寒颤。

pos.zh: 痛苦之事；折磨；被施加的处罚

senses.title: The act of causing pain
senses.definition: the act of making someone suffer physical or mental pain
senses.definitionCN: 使某人遭受身体或精神痛苦的行为
senses.example: The report condemned the deliberate infliction of pain on prisoners.
senses.exampleCN: 报告谴责了故意对囚犯施加痛苦的行为。
senses.why: The suffix -tion turns the verb into a noun naming the act, so infliction is the doing of what inflict describes.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -tion 把动词变为指称行为的名词，所以 infliction 就是 inflict 所描述的那个动作本身。

senses.title: The suffering that is imposed
senses.definition: the pain, hardship, or distress that someone is made to endure
senses.definitionCN: 某人被迫承受的痛苦、艰难或折磨
senses.example: He bore the infliction of years of silence without complaint.
senses.exampleCN: 他无怨言地承受多年沉默带来的痛苦。
senses.why: An act and its result are easily swapped, so the act sense extends to the pain which that act produces.
senses.whyCN: 行为与其结果常常互相替代，于是「施加」这一义项自然延伸到施加所产生的痛苦本身。

senses.title: The imposing of a punishment
senses.definition: the act or occasion of formally giving a penalty or legal sanction
senses.definitionCN: 正式给予惩罚或法律制裁的行为或场合
senses.example: The infliction of a fine was seen as too lenient.
senses.exampleCN: 判处罚金被认为过于宽大。
senses.why: Latin already used the word for putting a penalty on someone, and the noun keeps that legal layer.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语早已用这个词表示「把人置于刑罚之下」，名词形式保留了这一法律层次。

senses.title: A hardship that is imposed
senses.definition: an unwelcome burden, demand, or imposition placed on others
senses.definitionCN: 加于他人身上的不受欢迎的负担、要求或麻烦
senses.example: The endless forms were an infliction on every volunteer.
senses.exampleCN: 没完没了的表格给每位志愿者都添了负担。
senses.why: From imposed pain the word slides to imposed inconvenience, the lighter cousin of suffering.
senses.whyCN: 从被施加的痛苦出发，这个词滑向被强加的不便，这是痛苦较轻的一个兄弟。

senses.title: A wound or damage suffered
senses.definition: a loss, wound, or damaging event that has been caused to someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 已对某人或某物造成的损失、创伤或破坏事件
senses.example: The village never recovered from the infliction of the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村庄始终没能从洪水的重创中恢复过来。
senses.why: Anything that has been inflicted can be counted as a single infliction, so the noun names the event itself.
senses.whyCN: 凡是被施加的东西都可以作为一次 infliction 来计数，于是名词也用来指这个带来伤害的事件。

senses.title: Self-imposed suffering
senses.definition: suffering that a person brings upon himself or herself
senses.definitionCN: 一个人自己加给自己的痛苦
senses.example: Her infliction was choosing perfection over rest.
senses.exampleCN: 她的痛苦来自选择完美而放弃休息。
senses.why: When the doer and the sufferer are the same person, the word marks the habit of striking oneself.
senses.whyCN: 当施加者与承受者是同一个人时，这个词就标记出「自己打击自己」的这种习惯。

senses.title: Toil or wearisome labour
senses.definition: hard and wearisome labour, especially in older usage
senses.definitionCN: 艰苦而令人厌倦的劳动，多见于较早用法
senses.example: The old sailor called the long voyage an infliction.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老水手把漫长的航行称作一种苦役。
senses.why: Before it settled on pain, the word could cover any hard lot that life pressed on people.
senses.whyCN: 在意义固定为「痛苦」之前，这个词可以泛指生活压在人们身上的任何艰难处境。

intro.en: Infliction is the Latin-derived noun partner of inflict, formed from infligere plus the noun suffix -tion.
intro.cn: infliction 是 inflict 的拉丁语源名词伙伴，由 infligere 加名词后缀 -tion 构成。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning to strike, shared by the striking words of Latin and Greek.
items.cn: 一般认为存在表示「打击」的原始印欧语词根（重构形式），拉丁语与希腊语中的打击类词都与之相关。

items.en: Fligere means to strike, and infligere means to strike against or impose a penalty.
items.cn: fligere 意为「打击」，infligere 意为「打击于」或「施加刑罚」。

items.en: Noun formation in -tio turns the act of striking or imposing into a name.
items.cn: 以 -tio 结尾的名词构词法把「打击」或「施加」这一行为变成了名词。

items.en: The late Latin noun shape passes through French and settles into English as infliction.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语的名词形态经由法语传入，在英语中定型为 infliction。

items.en: The noun appears in English as a learned word for the act of causing pain or imposing penalty.
items.cn: 这个词在中古英语时期作为书面词汇出现，指施加痛苦或施加刑罚的行为。

items.en: Modern English also applies it to hardships, burdens, and self-imposed suffering.
items.cn: 现代英语还把它用于艰难、负担以及自己加给自己的痛苦。

note.en: Infliction is the noun of an act of harm, linked in form to inflict and inflicter and in meaning to suffering and imposition.
note.cn: infliction 指施害行为的名词，形式上与 inflict、inflicter 相连，意义上与「受苦」「强加」类词相邻。

normalIntro.en: Infliction is the -tion noun of inflict: the prefix in- means on, and the root means to strike.

normal.en: Replace -tion with nothing and you get inflict, the verb that puts pain on someone.
normal.cn: 把 -tion 去掉就回到 inflict，那是把痛苦施加给别人的动词。

normal.en: The infliction of pain is the most common pattern, where of names what is caused.
normal.cn: the infliction of pain 是最常见的搭配，of 后面接被施加的痛苦。

normal.en: Both infliction and affliction come from the same striking root: infliction is what is done, affliction is what is befallen.
normal.cn: infliction 与 affliction 出自同一表示打击的词根：前者是施加出去的行为，后者是被迫承受的苦难。

normal.en: Inflictive and inflicter keep the family near the verb.
normal.cn: inflictive 和 inflicter 让这个词族始终紧邻动词。

normal.en: Do not confuse infliction with fiction: one is pain, the other is invented story.
normal.cn: 别把 infliction 与 fiction 弄混：前者是痛苦，后者是编造的故事。

abstract.en: Picture a seal being lifted from the page, and the pressed mark left behind is the infliction.
abstract.cn: 想象印章从纸面抬起，留下的那个压痕就是 infliction。

abstract.en: Think of an orchestra player whose whole task is only to press down on another.
abstract.cn: 想象一个乐手，他的全部任务只是把某种力量按到别人身上，而按下去的那一下就是 infliction。

abstract.en: See a list of fines being read aloud, each item one more act of infliction.
abstract.cn: 想象有人逐条宣读罚单，每一条都是一次 infliction。

examples.en: The law forbids the infliction of unnecessary pain on animals.
examples.cn: 法律禁止对动物施加不必要的痛苦。

examples.en: His smile hid the infliction of a long illness.
examples.cn: 他的笑容掩盖了长期病痛带来的折磨。

examples.en: They treated the extra paperwork as a needless infliction on teachers.
examples.cn: 他们把那份额外的文书工作视为强加给教师的多余负担。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因弗力克申」——因为弗（不）肯放松的力气克住对方，再「申」诉也躲不开；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 fligere（打击）+ in-（在……之上）→ infligere（打击、施加）+ -tion（名词后缀）→ infliction，核心义「把打击施加出去的动作」。

sensesIntro.en: Infliction names the act of causing pain and, by extension, the pain itself, then punishment, burden, damage, self-imposed suffering, and older toil.
sensesIntro.cn: infliction 先指施加痛苦的行为，再转指被施加的痛苦本身，然后又延伸到惩罚、负担、损害、自我施加的痛苦，以及较早的「苦役」义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressing a blow down, and the pressed mark that remains.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把打击按下去，以及留下的那个压痕。

branches.en: The act and the damage it caused are two faces of one blow.
branches.cn: 施害的行为与它造成的损害是同一击的两面。

branches.en: What is endured is the noun turned inside out.
branches.cn: 被承受的痛苦是把动作名词翻到了另一面。

branches.en: A penalty is the formal, legal version of the blow.
branches.cn: 惩罚是这一击在正式制度与法律层面的版本。

branches.en: Burdens and toil are the mild, everyday forms of imposed hardship.
branches.cn: 负担与苦役是「被强加的艰难」在日常生活里的温和版本。

branches.en: The striker and the sufferer can be the same person.
branches.cn: 施加者与承受者可以是同一个人。

senses.title: A viral disease with fever and aches
senses.definition: an infectious disease caused by influenza viruses, marked by fever, muscle pain, and a dry cough
senses.definitionCN: 由流感病毒引起的传染病，表现为发热、肌肉酸痛和干咳
senses.example: Influenza is more serious than a common cold.
senses.exampleCN: 流感比普通感冒更严重。
senses.why: Italian influenza originally meant an influence, and a bad influence from the air was thought to bring the fever.
senses.whyCN: 意大利语 influenza 原意是「影响」，人们曾以为空气里不良的「影响」带来了高烧，于是这个词被用来指这种病。

senses.title: An outbreak or epidemic of flu
senses.titleCN: 一次流感流行；流感疫情
senses.definition: an outbreak or epidemic in which many people catch this disease at once
senses.definitionCN: 许多人同时患上这种病的暴发或流行
senses.example: A severe influenza swept through the town that winter.
senses.exampleCN: 那年冬天一场严重的流感横扫全城。
senses.why: The whole epidemic was once called one influence on a population, so the word can name the outbreak itself.
senses.whyCN: 人们曾把整场疫情看作作用于人群的一种「影响」，所以这个词也可以指这场流行本身。

senses.title: The disease of animals, especially birds
senses.definition: the same virus disease occurring in animals, especially poultry and pigs
senses.definitionCN: 发生在动物身上的同类病毒性疾病，尤其是禽类和猪
senses.example: Avian influenza can spread quickly through a flock.
senses.exampleCN: 禽流感可以在鸡群中迅速蔓延。
senses.why: Virology showed the virus jumps between species, and the word moved with it from people to animals.
senses.whyCN: 病毒学表明这类病毒会在物种之间跳跃，这个词于是随病毒一起从人扩展到动物。

senses.title: Miasma or a harmful emanation
senses.definition: in older medical writing, a harmful vapour or emanation thought to cause disease
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的医学文献中，被认为会致病的有害气体或「散发物」
senses.example: Physicians once blamed influenza on bad air from marshes.
senses.exampleCN: 医生们曾把流感归咎于沼泽散发的坏空气。
senses.why: Before germs were known, disease was explained as something flowing into the body from the sky or the earth.
senses.whyCN: 在认识细菌之前，疾病被解释为某种从天或地从外「流入」身体的东西。

senses.title: A sudden spread of an idea
senses.definition: in figurative use, something that spreads rapidly from person to person, like a disease
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法中指像疾病一样在人与人之间迅速蔓延的事物
senses.example: Jazz was called an influenza of the dance halls.
senses.exampleCN: 爵士乐曾被称作跳舞厅里流行的一场「流感」。
senses.why: Because the word already meant something spreading among all, it was borrowed for other contagious trends.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本已含有「在整个人群中扩散」的意思，于是被借来形容其他会传染的潮流。

senses.title: The influenza virus or its strain
senses.definition: the virus itself or one of its named strains, as in scientific and medical labels
senses.definitionCN: 病毒本身或某个命名的毒株，见于科学与医学标注
senses.example: Labs now sequence influenza A each season.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室现在每个流感季都会对甲型流感测序。
senses.why: Naming the disease by its cause is a short step, and the word shifted from illness to agent.
senses.whyCN: 用病因来称呼疾病只差一步，这个词于是从「病」滑向了「病原体」。

intro.en: Influenza comes from Italian, where it meant an influence, and the disease was once thought to be caused by an influence from the stars or the air.
intro.cn: influenza 来自意大利语，原义是「影响」，人们曾认为这种病是由星辰或空气带来的「影响」（流注）所致。

items.en: Influentia is formed from influere, to flow in, built on in- and fluere, to flow.
items.cn: influentia 由 influere（流入）构成，后者由 in- 与 fluere（流动）组合而成。

items.en: Astrologers spoke of an influenza or flowing-in of star power on earthly things.
items.cn: 中世纪占星学把星体之力向世间万物的「流注」称作 influenza。

items.en: Influenza becomes the Italian word for influence and for an epidemic, thought to be sent by an influence.
items.cn: influenza 成为意大利语中表示「影响」与「流行病」的词，人们认为传染病是由某种影响送来的。

items.en: The word is borrowed into English, where an influenza means an epidemic illness attributed to an influence.
items.cn: 这个词在十八世纪被借入英语，一种 influenza 指被认为由「影响」造成的流行性疾病。

items.en: The word narrows to the feverish viral illness we know today.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，这个词的意义收窄为今天所熟知的发热性病毒疾病。

items.en: The shortened form flu appears in the nineteenth century and now carries most everyday use.
items.cn: 缩写 flu 出现在十九世纪，如今承载了绝大部分日常用法。

note.en: Influenza is the long medical name of flu, close in form to the influence family and in meaning to other respiratory infections.
note.cn: influenza 是 flu 的正式医学全称，形式上接近 influence 一族，意义上与其他呼吸道感染相邻。

entries.definition: the power to affect how things develop
entries.definitionCN: 影响；影响力（与流感同源）

entries.definition: having great power to affect decisions
the everyday short name for influenza
a mild illness that makes you sneeze and cough
a tiny infectious agent that reproduces inside cells
a disease that spreads quickly among many people

normalIntro.en: Influenza is built on the flowing root flu-, the very root that gives influence its sense of flowing in.
normalIntro.cn: influenza 由表示「流动」的词根 flu- 构成，influence 的「流入」之意也出自同一个词根。

normal.en: Influence and influenza share a history: both once described something flowing into people from the stars.
normal.cn: influence 与 influenza 有同一段历史：二者都曾描述从星辰流入人体的东西。

normal.en: The everyday English word is simply flu, and the long form belongs to doctors and official reports.
normal.cn: 日常英语直接说 flu，长篇的正式形式多出现在医生和官方报告中。

normal.en: Catch influenza means to fall ill with it, and the phrase catches the sense of catching what is in the air.
normal.cn: catch influenza 表示染上流感，这个搭配也保留了「染上空气中漂浮之物」的画面。

normal.en: Influenza virus, influenza vaccine, and influenza season are the three most common partners.
normal.cn: influenza virus、influenza vaccine、influenza season 是三个最常见的搭配伙伴。

normal.en: Compare cold and influenza: a cold creeps, influenza hits in a single night with fever.
normal.cn: 对比 cold 与 influenza：感冒慢慢来，流感却常在一夜之间以高烧袭来。

abstract.en: Picture cold mist rolling down a street and every window going lit with fever.
abstract.cn: 想象冷雾沿街滚下，一扇扇窗户里同时亮起了高烧的灯。

abstract.en: Imagine one sneeze in a bus, and the bus slowly turning into a sickroom.
abstract.cn: 想象公交车上一声喷嚏，整辆车慢慢变成一间病房。

abstract.en: See a map where measles-like red dots leap from city to city along flight lines.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，红色小点沿着航线从一个城市跳到另一个城市。

examples.en: She was off work for a week with influenza.
examples.cn: 她因流感休假一周。

examples.en: The influenza vaccine is updated every year to match new strains.
examples.cn: 流感疫苗每年都会更新，以匹配新的毒株。

examples.en: Avian influenza raised fears of a wider outbreak.
examples.cn: 禽流感引发了人们对疫情进一步扩大的担忧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阴风流恩咋」——寒气阴风一吹，病毒到处乱窜，咳得人直喊「咋」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 influere（流入，in 在内 + fluere 流动）→ 中世纪占星「流注」influentia → 意大利语 influenza（影响；流行病）→ 英语 influenza，核心义「从外面流入身体的东西」。

sensesIntro.en: Influenza starts as a single viral illness, extends to the epidemic it causes, to the same disease in animals, back to the old idea of a harmful emanation, then to figurative contagion and to the virus itself.
sensesIntro.cn: influenza 首先指一种病毒性急性病，再扩展到它引发的流行疫情，又指动物所患的同类疾病，然后回溯到旧观念中的「疫气」，最后走向比喻性的蔓延以及病毒本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mist flowing in from outside and settling on a whole town at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：从外面流入的雾气，同时笼罩整座城镇。

branches.en: The illness and the virus it comes from share one name in modern usage.
branches.cn: 疾病与引起它的病毒在现代用法中共用同一个名字。

branches.en: One epidemic is one flow of illness over a whole population.
branches.cn: 一场疫情就是病痛对整个人群的一次「涌流」。

branches.en: The same virus crosses from people to animals and back again.
branches.cn: 同一种病毒会从人传给动物，再传回人类。

branches.en: The old belief in bad air is the earliest stage of the word.
branches.cn: 关于「坏空气」的旧观念是这个词最早的阶段。

branches.en: Anything that spreads fast can borrow the disease metaphor.
branches.cn: 任何迅速扩散的事物都可以借用一个疾病的比喻。

intro.en: Influenza is built on in- and the flowing root fluere, with the -enza ending carried over from Italian beside its English relatives influence and influential.
intro.cn: influenza 由前缀 in- 与表示「流动」的词根 fluere 构成，词尾 -enza 来自意大利语，英语中与之相邻的是 influence 和 influential。

latinIntro.en: Latin fluere means to flow, and influere means to flow into; influentia is the noun for such a flow.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fluere 意为「流动」，influere 意为「流入」，influentia 就是表示这种流入的名词。

items.example: The prefix in- means the flow comes into the body.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 表示气流「进入」身体。

items.example: Fluere gives the image of something running like water.
items.exampleCN: fluere 提供了像水一样流淌的意象。

items.example: Influere describes the air flooding into a house.
items.exampleCN: influere 描绘空气涌入房屋。

items.example: Influentia was used for a flowing in of a power or fluid.
items.exampleCN: influentia 曾被用来指某种力量或流质的流入。

items.example: Influence keeps the older, non-medical sense of the same word.
items.exampleCN: influence 保留了同一个词较早的非医学含义。

items.example: The suffix -ial forms influential from influence.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ial 由 influence 构成 influential。

items.meaningCN: 随借用一同进入的意大利语式词尾
items.example: The ending -enza travels with the word from Italian.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -enza 随着这个词从意大利语一起进入英语。

items.example: The suffix -al forms influenzal.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 构成 influenzal。

items.example: Affluent shares the flowing root with another prefix.
items.exampleCN: affluent 用另一个前缀共用「流动」词根。

items.example: Fluent calls the same flowing image a smooth speech.
items.exampleCN: fluent 把同一个流动意象用于流畅的言语。
