流感的日常简称

definition_zh: 大量涌入；流入；涌进的人或物；汇集
definition_en: the arrival of a large number of people or things at the same time and place
core_image: 潮水般的人群和物资，同时涌进同一个入口
scene: 新学年开始前，外地学生和行李一起涌进小城。A sudden influx of students filled every hostel in the town.
sceneCN: 这里 influx 是「大量涌入、涌入的人或物」（第 1 个义项：许多人或事物同时到来）；句意：学生突然大量涌入，住满了镇上每一家旅馆。

pos.zh: 涌入；涌入的人或物；流入；汇集

derivatives.zh: 由 influx 加 -ion 构成的罕见名词，义为「流入；涌入」；现代英语几乎不用，只在旧词典与医学旧文献中偶见
同根词：拉丁语前缀 ef-（向外）与 fluxus（流动）结合，义为「流出」；极罕见的技术用词
同根词：前缀 re-（向后）与 fluxus 结合，义为「回流」；现代主要用于化学的「回流」与医学的胃酸反流
同根词：前缀 con-（共同）与 fluxus 结合，义为「汇流；汇集」；是 confluence 的较古旧拼法

senses.title: A surge of many arrivals
senses.titleCN: 大量涌入；涌入的人或物
senses.definition: the arrival of a large number of people or things at one place in a short time
senses.definitionCN: 许多人和事物在短时间里大量到达同一个地方
senses.example: The festival brought a huge influx of visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 节庆活动带来了大量游客涌入。
senses.why: Latin fluere means to flow, and the prefix in- directs that flow inward, so an influx is a tide of arrivals pouring in at once.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 fluere 意为「流动」，前缀 in- 把流动指向内部，所以 influx 就是同时大量灌进来的「到达之潮」。

senses.title: Money flowing in
senses.definition: money or resources flowing into a place or organization
senses.definitionCN: 金钱或资源流进某个地方或组织
senses.example: The new port channeled an influx of foreign capital.
senses.exampleCN: 新港口引来大量外国资金流入。
senses.why: The same inward flood image applies to money: capital flows in just as people do, so the word covers both.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「向内灌注」的画面也适用于金钱：资金和人一样流进来，所以这个词同时覆盖两者。

senses.title: A stream joining a body of water
senses.definition: the point where a stream of water flows into a larger river or lake
senses.definitionCN: 溪水流进大河或湖泊的汇入处
senses.example: The marsh grows where the influx reaches the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 沼泽就长在水流汇入湖泊的地方。
senses.why: This is the most literal sense: water flowing into a larger body, the original physical picture behind the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是最字面的义项：水流进更大的水体，也就是这个词背后原本的物理画面。

senses.title: An influx of ideas or influence
senses.titleCN: 大量传入的思想或影响
senses.definition: the arrival of new ideas, influences, or customs in a place
senses.definitionCN: 新思想、新影响或新风尚大量进入某个地方
senses.example: Trade routes brought an influx of fresh ideas.
senses.exampleCN: 商路带来了新思想的大量传入。
senses.why: Since flow does not need water, new ideas can also flood into a culture, and the colloquial horde sense is deliberately not used here.
senses.whyCN: 既然流动不一定需要水，新思想也能灌进一种文化里；这里刻意不采用口语中「蜂群般的人群」那一说法。

senses.title: A point where things meet
senses.definition: a place where several streams or forces come together
senses.definitionCN: 好几条水流或几股力量汇聚到一起的地方
senses.example: The old town grew at the influx of two rivers.
senses.exampleCN: 这座古镇在两河交汇处发展起来。
senses.why: Where several streams arrive at once they meet, so the point of arrival turns into a meeting point.
senses.whyCN: 好几条水流同时到达就会相碰，于是「到达之处」很自然地变成了「交汇之处」。

intro.en: Influx is built from the Latin prefix in- (into) and fluxus (a flowing). English took it straight from the Latin noun influxus or a later Latin borrowing.
intro.cn: influx 由拉丁语前缀 in-（进入）与 fluxus（流动）构成，英语直接从拉丁语名词 influxus 或后世拉丁语借用而来。

items.en: Fluere means to flow, and its past participle fluxus means a flowing.
items.cn: fluere 意为流动，其过去分词 fluxus 意为「流动」。

items.en: Influxus means a flowing in, formed with the prefix in-, into.
items.cn: influxus 意为「流入」，由前缀 in-（进入）构成。

items.en: Learned Latin influxus enters English as a noun for a flowing in of water.
items.cn: 16 世纪，学术拉丁语 influxus 作为「水流入」的名词进入英语。

items.en: The word extends from water to people, goods, and money arriving in quantity.
items.cn: 17 世纪起，这个词从水扩展到大量到来的人、货物与金钱。

items.en: Modern journalism uses it for tourist rushes, capital flows, and new ideas.
items.cn: 现代新闻语言用它指游客潮、资金流入与新思想的涌入。

note.en: Influx belongs to the Latin flowing family of fluere, which gives fluent, fluid, flux, and confluence. It is close to words for inflow and arrival.
note.cn: influx 属于拉丁语 fluere（流动）词族，同族有 fluent、fluid、flux 与 confluence；它与表示流入、到达的词义场相邻。

entries.definition: a continuous flowing or changing
entries.definitionCN: 不断的流动或变化；flux 是同根名词

entries.definition: the place where two rivers flow together
entries.definitionCN: 汇流处；两条河交汇的地方

entries.definition: the movement of something into a place
entries.definitionCN: 流入；inflow 与 influx 都含 in-

entries.definition: a sudden inward rush
a regular rise and fall, or a large amount of something
the act of reaching a place

normalIntro.en: Influx pairs the prefix in- with the Latin flow noun flux: an inward flood, whether of water, people, or money.
normalIntro.cn: influx 是前缀 in-（进入）与拉丁语流动名词 flux 的组合：向内灌进的一股洪水，可以是水、人，也可以是钱。

normal.en: Flux in English means a flowing or changing state, and influx adds the inward direction.
normal.cn: 英语 flux 意为流动或不断变化，influx 给它加上「向内」的方向。

normal.en: An influx of tourists is a rush of visitors, not a single guest.
normal.cn: an influx of tourists 是一股游客潮，而不是单独一位客人。

normal.en: Capital influx describes money pouring into a market.
normal.cn: capital influx 描述资金涌入市场。

normal.en: A sudden influx is the standard collocation for a sharp and quick arrival.
normal.cn: a sudden influx 是表示「突然涌入」的标准搭配。

normal.en: Compare inflow: inflow is neutral and continuous, while influx suggests a large amount arriving at one time.
normal.cn: 对比 inflow：inflow 中性而持续，influx 则暗示一次到达的巨大数量。

abstract.en: Picture floodgates opening and a crowd pouring through at once.
abstract.cn: 想象水闸一开，人群同时涌过同一道门。

abstract.en: Picture coins tumbling down a funnel into a jar.
abstract.cn: 想象硬币从漏斗里哗哗倒进一只罐子。

abstract.en: Picture a stream pouring itself into a wide lake.
abstract.cn: 想象一条溪流把自己灌进一片大湖。

examples.en: The new university caused an influx of young workers.
examples.cn: 这所新大学引来了大量年轻劳动者涌入。

examples.en: Investors were encouraged by the influx of funds.
examples.cn: 资金的流入让投资者受到鼓舞。

examples.en: Every summer the coast expects a large influx of holidaymakers.
examples.cn: 每年夏天，沿海地区都预料会有大量度假者涌入。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因福利」——因为福利好，大家都往这里涌进来；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（进入）+ fluere（流动）→ fluxus（流动）→ influxus（流入）→ 英语 influx，核心义「向内涌进」。

sensesIntro.en: Influx starts from a literal flow of water into a larger body, widens to a flood of people and money, and finally softens into any meeting of streams or influences.
sensesIntro.cn: influx 从字面上「水流入更大水体」起步，扩展到人与钱财的大量涌入，最后弱化为水流或影响的任何交汇。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crowd and its goods pouring in through one gate.
core.cn: 核心意象：人群和物资同时从一道门涌进来。

branches.en: People and things arriving in a surge is the main modern sense.
branches.cn: 人或物成批到达，是现代最主要的义项。

branches.en: Money flowing into a market repeats the same image.
branches.cn: 资金流进市场，重复的是同一个意象。

branches.en: Water entering a lake keeps the original physical picture.
branches.cn: 水汇入湖泊，保留了原本的物理画面。

branches.en: Ideas and customs can flood in just as water does.
branches.cn: 思想和风俗也能像水一样灌进来。

branches.en: A place of arrival easily becomes a meeting point of streams.
branches.cn: 「到达之处」很容易变成「溪流交汇之处」。

intro.en: Influx is a Latin compound: the prefix in- meaning into, plus the noun fluxus from fluere. The same root creates flux, inflow, and confluence.
intro.cn: influx 是拉丁语复合词：前缀 in- 表示「进入」，加上由 fluere 派生的名词 fluxus。同一词根还造出 flux、inflow 与 confluence。

latinIntro.en: Latin fluere means to flow and fluxus means a flowing; the prefix in- adds the direction inward.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fluere 意为流动，fluxus 意为流动本身；前缀 in- 补上「向内」的方向。

items.example: The prefix in- makes an inward movement.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 表示向内运动。

items.example: Fluere is the source verb of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: fluere 是整个词族的源动词。

items.example: Fluxus is the flowing noun.
items.exampleCN: fluxus 是表示「流动」的名词。

items.example: Influx keeps the compound meaning.
items.exampleCN: influx 保留了复合词义。

items.meaningCN: 以 s、x 结尾时加 -es 构成复数
items.example: Influx takes -es to make influxes.
items.exampleCN: influx 加 -es 构成复数 influxes。

items.example: Influxion is a rare noun built on this pattern.
items.exampleCN: influxion 是照这一模式构成的罕见名词。

items.example: The root flu- appears in fluent and fluid.
items.exampleCN: 词根 flu- 出现在 fluent 与 fluid 中。

items.example: Conflux is an old spelling of confluence.
items.exampleCN: conflux 是 confluence 的古老拼法。

items.example: Flux is the bare noun without a prefix.
items.exampleCN: flux 是不带前缀的裸名词。

items.example: Reflux adds the direction back.
items.exampleCN: reflux 加上「向后」的方向。

definition_zh: 次声；次声波；次声效应
definition_en: sound waves below the range of normal human hearing
core_image: 耳朵听不见的极低音，像整座楼板在无声地颤动
scene: 地震前大象不安地走动，它们能感觉到人类听不见的低音。Elephants can sense the infrasound of a distant earthquake.
sceneCN: 这里 infrasound 是「次声、次声波」（第 1 个义项：低于人耳听力下限的声波）；句意：大象能感知远处地震产生的次声。

derivatives.zh: 以 infra-（低于）为前缀、带形容词后缀 -ic 构成的同族形容词，义为「次声的；低于可听频率的」，常用来修饰 wave 等名词
同一个前缀 infra-（低于）的另一种组合：infra- 加 red，义为「红外线的」，指频率低于可见红光的辐射
相对概念：前缀 ultra-（超出）替换 infra-，义为「超声」，指频率高于人耳可听上限的声波
近义概念：sub-（在下）+ sonic（声音的），义为「亚音速的」，指速度低于当地声速

senses.title: Sound below hearing
senses.definition: sound waves with a frequency below the normal limit of human hearing
senses.definitionCN: 频率低于人耳正常听力下限的声波
senses.example: Scientists record the infrasound made by distant volcanic eruptions.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家记录远处火山喷发产生的次声。
senses.why: Infra- means below and sound is the thing itself, so infrasound is literally the sound lying beneath what ears can catch.
senses.whyCN: infra- 表示「低于」，sound 就是声音本身，所以 infrasound 字面上就是「躺在耳朵能捕捉的范围之下的声音」。

senses.title: A tool for studying the earth
senses.definition: the field of study and monitoring that uses such waves
senses.definitionCN: 利用这类声波进行研究与监测的领域
senses.example: Infrasound is now part of monitoring networks.
senses.exampleCN: 次声如今已是监测网络的一部分。
senses.why: Once waves below hearing became measurable, they were put to work in earthquake and explosion detection, so the word also names the practice.
senses.whyCN: 当低于听阈的声波可以被测量之后，它们就被用于地震与爆炸探测，于是这个词也指这门实践。

senses.title: Effects on the body
senses.definition: the unpleasant effects of such waves on people or animals
senses.definitionCN: 这类声波对人畜造成的不适反应
senses.example: Wind turbines raised questions about infrasound.
senses.exampleCN: 风力涡轮机引发了关于次声的疑问。
senses.why: Because people cannot hear the wave but may still feel it, the word also names the vague discomfort it causes.
senses.whyCN: 人虽然听不见这种波，却可能仍然感觉到它，于是这个词也指它带来的那种说不清的不适。

senses.title: How animals use it
senses.definition: the use of these waves by animals to communicate or sense danger
senses.definitionCN: 动物利用这类声波交流或感知危险
senses.example: Elephants use infrasound to warn the herd.
senses.exampleCN: 大象用次声向象群传递警报。
senses.why: Animals hear far below the human limit, so the same low waves become a channel for warning and contact.
senses.whyCN: 动物的听觉远低于人类的下限，于是同一种低波成了传递警报与联络的通道。

intro.en: Infrasound is a modern compound: the Latin-derived prefix infra- (below) joins the English noun sound. The term belongs to twentieth-century acoustics.
intro.cn: infrasound 是现代复合词：拉丁语来源的前缀 infra-（低于）与英语名词 sound 组合而成，属于二十世纪声学术语。

items.en: Latin infra means below or beneath, and English keeps it as a prefix.
items.cn: 拉丁语 infra 意为「在……之下」，英语把它保留为前缀。

items.en: Sound comes from Latin sonus, which also gave the older English word soun.
items.cn: sound 源自拉丁语 sonus，它也给英语带来了古旧的拼写 soun。

items.en: Scientific Latin uses infra- in compounds such as infrasonic.
items.cn: 20 世纪的科学拉丁语用 infra- 造出 infrasonic 等复合词。

items.en: Infrasound is coined for waves below twenty hertz.
items.cn: 现代英语造出 infrasound，指频率低于二十赫兹的声波。

items.en: After the 1990s the word spreads into ecology, noise policy, and animal biology.
items.cn: 二十世纪九十年代以后，这个词扩展到生态学、噪声政策与动物生物学。

note.en: Infrasound is built with the prefix infra-, the partner of ultra-, and it sits in the family of wave words such as ultrasound and infrared.
note.cn: infrasound 由前缀 infra- 构成，与 ultra- 相对，处在 ultrasound、infrared 这类「波」词族之中。

entries.definition: of or about waves below hearing
entries.definitionCN: 次声的；低于可听频率的

entries.definition: sound above the hearing range
entries.definitionCN: 超声；与 infrasound 前缀相反

entries.definition: radiation below red light
entries.definitionCN: 红外线的；同为 infra- 构词

entries.definition: slower than the speed of sound
the science of sound
a long low continuous sound

normalIntro.en: Infrasound is infra- (below) plus sound: the sound that lies below the hearing floor.
normalIntro.cn: infrasound 是 infra-（低于）加 sound（声音）：躺在听觉地板之下的声音。

normal.en: Infra- appears in infrared, so infra- always points below a threshold.
normal.cn: infra- 也出现在 infrared 中，所以它总是指「低于某个界限」。

normal.en: Ultrasound is its partner: ultra- is above hearing, infra- is below it.
normal.cn: ultrasound 是它的搭档：ultra- 在听阈之上，infra- 在听阈之下。

normal.en: Infrasound monitoring is the standard phrase for the recording network.
normal.cn: infrasound monitoring 是记录网络的标准说法。

normal.en: Elephants are famous users of infrasound for long range warning.
normal.cn: 大象是以次声进行远距离警报的著名使用者。

normal.en: The plural is infrasounds, but the uncountable use without a plural is more common.
normal.cn: 复数是 infrasounds，但不用复数的不可数用法更常见。

abstract.en: Put a hand on a speaker and feel the silent thump.
abstract.cn: 把手按在音箱上，感受那种听不见的轰击。

abstract.en: Imagine an earthquake drumming below the ground like a hidden heart.
abstract.cn: 想象地震在地底像一颗隐藏的心脏那样擂动。

abstract.en: Imagine an elephant calling in a voice too low for human ears.
abstract.cn: 想象一头大象用一种人类听不到的极低嗓音在呼叫。

examples.en: Volcano monitoring relies on infrasound from eruptions.
examples.cn: 火山监测依赖喷发产生的次声。

examples.en: Some insects react to infrasound before a storm.
examples.cn: 有些昆虫在暴风雨前会对次声作出反应。

examples.en: Engineers measured the infrasound around the new wind farm.
examples.cn: 工程师测量了新风电场的次声。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「音弗劳音」——音量太低了，耳朵里听不到，只能「弗」了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 infra（在……之下）+ 英语 sound（声音，源自拉丁语 sonus）→ 现代英语 infrasound，核心义「听阈之下的声波」。

sensesIntro.en: Infrasound first names the wave itself, then widens to the monitoring field, the uncomfortable effects it has, and the way animals use it.
sensesIntro.cn: infrasound 先指声波本身，再扩展到监测领域、它引起的不适，以及动物对它的利用。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a very low hum that shakes the floor while the ears hear nothing.
core.cn: 核心意象：极低沉的嗡鸣震着楼板，耳朵却什么都听不见。

branches.en: The wave itself below the hearing floor is the main sense.
branches.cn: 听阈之下的声波本身是主要义项。

branches.en: Used to detect events, the word names a monitoring field.
branches.cn: 用来探测事件时，这个词指一个监测领域。

branches.en: Feeling without hearing explains the discomfort sense.
branches.cn: 「听得见的不适、听不见的声音」解释了不适的义项。

branches.en: Animals reaching lower frequencies turns the term into a way of hearing.
branches.cn: 动物能接收到更低的频率，让这个词变成一种听觉方式。

branches.en: The wave and the network that records it share one image.
branches.cn: 声波和记录它的网络共享一个意象。

intro.en: Infrasound combines the prefix infra- with the English noun sound; the mirror prefix ultra- gives ultrasound, and the same family holds infrasonic.
intro.cn: infrasound 由前缀 infra- 与英语名词 sound 组合；镜像前缀 ultra- 给出 ultrasound，同一词族还有 infrasonic。

latinIntro.en: Latin infra means below; it became a productive English prefix in words such as infrared and infrastructure.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 infra 意为「在……之下」，它成为英语中高产的前缀，见于 infrared 与 infrastructure。

items.example: The prefix infra- lowers a threshold.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 infra- 把界限降低。

items.example: Ultra- is the mirror of infra-.
items.exampleCN: ultra- 是 infra- 的镜像。

items.example: Sub- also means below in some words.
items.exampleCN: sub- 在有些词里也表示「低于」。

items.example: Sonus is the Latin source of sound.
items.exampleCN: sonus 是 sound 的拉丁语来源。

items.example: Audire underlies audible and audio.
items.exampleCN: audire 是 audible 与 audio 的底子。

items.example: The suffix -ic forms infrasonic.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ic 构成 infrasonic。

items.example: Infrasonic describes the waves, not the noun.
items.exampleCN: infrasonic 描述的是波，而不是名词。

items.example: Infrared is a sister compound with infra-.
items.exampleCN: infrared 是同样用 infra- 的姐妹复合词。

items.meaning: the basic systems of a place
items.example: Infrastructure shows the prefix at work.
items.exampleCN: infrastructure 展示了这个前缀的用法。

items.example: Ultrasound pairs with infrasound.
items.exampleCN: ultrasound 与 infrasound 成对。

definition_zh: 侵犯；违反；违犯；侵害；触及界限
definition_en: to break a law, rule, or right, or to go beyond a limit
core_image: 一条画在地上的界线被人一脚踏过去
scene: 版权所有者发现有人擅自使用自己的作品。The publisher said the new app infringed its copyright.
sceneCN: 这里 infringe 是「侵犯、侵害（权利）」（第 3 个义项：侵害他人的权利或版权）；句意：出版方说这款新应用侵犯了他们的版权。

pos.zh: 侵犯；违反；侵害；触及界限

derivatives.zh: 动词 infringe 加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「违反；侵犯；侵害」
动词 infringe 加表人后缀 -er 构成，义为「侵权者；违反者」
现在分词用作形容词，义为「构成侵权的；违规的」
加前缀 non-（不）构成的否定形式，义为「不侵权的」；属法律与技术文书的构词

senses.title: To go beyond a limit
senses.definition: to go past the edge of what is allowed
senses.definitionCN: 越过被允许的边界
senses.example: Any extra chair would infringe on the narrow path beside the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 再多一把椅子就会挤占到书桌旁那条窄路；此处 infringe 意在描写越界。
senses.why: The core image is stepping over a drawn line, so the earliest use describes physically going past an edge that should be respected.
senses.whyCN: 核心画面就是踏过一条画在地上的界线，所以这个词先描述实物上越过本该被尊重的边界。

senses.title: To break a rule or law
senses.definition: to break a law, rule, or agreement
senses.definitionCN: 破坏法律、规则或协议
senses.example: Drivers who infringe the speed limit will be fined.
senses.exampleCN: 超速违反限速规定的司机将被罚款。
senses.why: A law is a line drawn by the community, so breaking it is the same act of crossing that line.
senses.whyCN: 法律是社会共同画的界线，违反它本质上就是同一种越线动作。

senses.title: To violate rights
senses.definition: to harm the rights of a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 损害某人或某群体的权利
senses.example: The new rule infringes the rights of tenants.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定侵害了租户的权利。
senses.why: Rights are invisible boundary lines too, so stepping on them becomes infringement of rights, the most common modern use.
senses.whyCN: 权利也是看不见的界线，踩上去就成了「侵害权利」，这是现代最常见的用法。

senses.title: To invade privacy
senses.definition: to interfere with the private life of someone
senses.definitionCN: 干涉某人的私生活
senses.example: Cameras in the lift may infringe the privacy of residents.
senses.exampleCN: 电梯里的摄像头可能侵扰住户的隐私。
senses.why: Privacy is the most personal boundary of all, so reaching into it is an intrusion felt as interference.
senses.whyCN: 隐私是最个人的一道界，把手伸进去就是被感受为「干涉」的侵扰。

senses.title: To break a legal right formally
senses.definition: to break a legal right such as a patent or copyright, especially by copying
senses.definitionCN: 以复制等方式破坏专利、版权等法定权利
senses.example: Selling the copies would infringe the patent.
senses.exampleCN: 出售这些复制品会侵犯该专利。
senses.why: Legal systems draw formal protected lines, and copying across them is infringement in the strict legal sense used in court.
senses.whyCN: 法律体系画出受到正式保护的界线，越过它去复制，就是法庭上严格意义上的侵权。

intro.en: Infringe comes from Latin infringere, to break or dash against, formed from in- (against) and frangere (to break), the root of fracture.
intro.cn: infringe 来自拉丁语 infringere（打碎、撞上），由 in-（反对、抵着）与 frangere（打破）构成；fracture 也出自同一词根。

items.en: Frangere means to break, and it lies behind fracture and fragile.
items.cn: frangere 意为「打破」，fracture 与 fragile 都出自它。

items.en: Infringere means to break, shatter, or dash against something.
items.cn: infringere 意为打碎、击碎或撞在某物上。

items.en: Legal Latin in infringere gives English the recorded verb in the early sixteenth century.
items.cn: 十六世纪初，法律拉丁语 in infringere 给英语带来了有记录的动词形式。

items.en: The verb shifts from physical breaking toward breaking a law or right.
items.cn: 十七世纪起，这个动词从物理上的「打破」转向「打破法律或权利」。

items.en: Copyright and patent law make infringement a technical legal term today.
items.cn: 如今的版权法与专利法把 infringement 变成专门的法律术语。

note.en: Infringe shares the Latin breaking root of fracture and fragile, and it lies close to words for breaking rules and trespassing.
note.cn: infringe 与 fracture、fragile 共享拉丁语「打破」词根，并与表示违规、侵入的词义场相邻。

entries.definition: the breaking of a law or right
entries.definitionCN: 违反；侵权；由 infringe 加 -ment 构成

entries.definition: a break in a bone or hard object
easily broken
entries.definitionCN: 易碎的；与 frangere 同根

entries.definition: to break a law or rule
a failure to keep a law or promise
to enter land without permission

normalIntro.en: Infringe is in- plus the Latin breaking root of fracture: to break a line, a law, or a right.
normalIntro.cn: infringe 是 in- 加上 fracture 的拉丁「打破」词根：打破界线、法律或权利。

normal.en: The breaking root also gives fracture, so infringe is about smashing a boundary.
normal.cn: 这个「打破」词根也给出 fracture，所以 infringe 说的是砸坏界限。

normal.en: Infringe on is the usual pattern before privacy or freedom.
normal.cn: 在 privacy、freedom 之前常用 infringe on。

normal.en: Infringe a law or a right takes no on or upon.
normal.cn: infringe a law 或 infringe a right 后面不加 on 或 upon。

normal.en: Infringement is the noun used in copyright and patent disputes.
normal.cn: infringement 是版权与专利纠纷中的常用名词。

normal.en: Compare violate: violate is broader, while infringe is often used for rights, patents, and narrow rules.
normal.cn: 对比 violate：violate 范围更宽，infringe 常用于权利、专利与细小的规定。

abstract.en: Picture a foot crossing a chalk line on the floor.
abstract.cn: 想象一只脚跨过画在地上的粉笔线。

abstract.en: Picture a hand reaching into another person private folder.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸进别人私人的文件夹。

abstract.en: Picture a copy of a book rolling off the press without permission.
abstract.cn: 想象一本未经许可的书从印刷机上滚下来。

examples.en: The app infringes on users privacy and must be changed.
examples.cn: 这款应用侵犯了用户的隐私，必须做出修改。

examples.en: Anyone who infringes these rules will lose the licence.
examples.cn: 任何人违反这些规定都会失去执照。

examples.en: The court found that the design infringed a patent.
examples.cn: 法院认定这款设计侵犯了一项专利。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因佛林纪」——因为不守佛家的戒律，被记上一笔违规账；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（反对、抵着）+ frangere（打破）→ infringere（打碎、撞上）→ 英语 infringe，核心义「越过界线、破坏规则或权利」。

sensesIntro.en: Infringe grows from physically stepping over a limit to breaking a written law, then to violating rights or privacy, and finally to the formal legal breaking of a patent or copyright.
sensesIntro.cn: infringe 从现实中踏过界线起步，发展为违反成文法，再到侵犯权利与隐私，最后指法律意义上对专利、版权的正式侵害。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foot crossing a line drawn on the ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只脚跨过画在地上的界线。

branches.en: Steps past an edge kept the physical image.
branches.cn: 越过边沿这一步保留了物理画面。

branches.en: A rule as a drawn line covers the legal sense.
branches.cn: 把规则看作画的线，就覆盖了违法义项。

branches.en: Invisible rights turn trespass into harm to people.
branches.cn: 看不见的权利让「越界」变成了对人的伤害。

branches.en: The most personal border is privacy.
branches.cn: 最私人的边界就是隐私。

branches.en: Rights and patents are both formal lines that courts defend.
branches.cn: 权利和专利都是法院守护的正式界线。

intro.en: Infringe is in- plus the Latin breaking root frangere, which also shows in fracture and fragile. Agreement and law are its usual objects.
intro.cn: infringe 是 in- 加上拉丁语「打破」词根 frangere，后者也见于 fracture 与 fragile。契约和法律是它常见的宾语。

latinIntro.en: Latin frangere means to break, and infringere means to break or dash against something.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 frangere 意为打破，infringere 意为打碎或撞在某物上。

items.example: The prefix in- here means against.
items.exampleCN: 这里的前缀 in- 表示「抵着、反对」。

items.example: Frangere is the breaking verb at the core.
items.exampleCN: frangere 是核心的「打破」动词。

items.example: The root fract- appears in fracture.
items.exampleCN: 词根 fract- 出现在 fracture 中。

items.example: Infringere is the direct source verb.
items.exampleCN: infringere 是直接来源动词。

items.example: The suffix -ment forms infringement.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ment 构成 infringement。

items.example: The suffix -er forms infringer.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 infringer。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或其形容词用法
items.example: The suffix -ing forms infringing.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 infringing。

items.example: The prefix non- makes non-infringing.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 non- 构成 non-infringing。

items.example: Fracture shows the same breaking root.
items.exampleCN: fracture 展示了同一个「打破」词根。

items.example: Fragile is the adjective of the same root.
items.exampleCN: fragile 是同词根的形容词。

items.example: Infrangible adds the negative in-.
items.exampleCN: infrangible 加上否定前缀 in-。

definition_zh: 使极其愤怒；激怒；惹恼；也指狂怒的
definition_en: to make someone extremely angry, or to be filled with great anger
core_image: 一簇火苗落进干柴，火势猛地窜起来，人也被烧得满脸通红
scene: 谈判拖到深夜，对方一句轻慢的话把一直克制的同事彻底激怒了。A careless remark from the other side infuriated the normally calm negotiator.
sceneCN: 这里 infuriate 是「使极其愤怒、激怒」（第 1 个义项：让某人暴怒）；句意：对方一句不经意的话把一向冷静的谈判代表激怒了。

derivatives.zh: 令人愤怒的；恼人的
令人恼火地；气人地
暴怒；激怒他人的状态
狂怒；暴怒（同根名词）

senses.title: To make someone furious
senses.definition: to cause someone to become extremely angry and lose control of their temper
senses.definitionCN: 使某人变得极其愤怒、难以克制脾气
senses.example: The broken promises infuriated the villagers.
senses.exampleCN: 一次次落空的承诺让村民愤怒至极。
senses.why: The word is built on the Latin noun furia, rage, so infuriating is pouring that rage into another person.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在拉丁语名词 furia（狂怒）之上，使某人 infuriate 就是把那股怒火灌注到别人身上。

senses.title: Filled with rage
senses.definition: extremely angry, as in a state of boiling rage
senses.definitionCN: 处于狂怒状态、愤怒到极点
senses.example: He was infuriated by the unfair ruling.
senses.exampleCN: 那条不公的裁决让他怒不可遏。
senses.why: The participle takes on an adjective sense: the person has been filled with the Latin furia and now shows it.
senses.whyCN: 分词形式取得形容词义：人被拉丁语 furia 填满之后，就表现出狂怒的样子。

senses.title: Something that causes anger
senses.definition: annoying or provoking because it repeatedly frustrates patience
senses.definitionCN: 因反复消磨耐心而令人气恼、令人愤怒
senses.example: The infuriating noise kept the whole floor awake.
senses.exampleCN: 那恼人的噪音让整层楼的人都睡不着。
senses.why: Objects and events can also carry the rage, so the word describes whatever stirs anger in the people around it.
senses.whyCN: 物件和事情也能携带那股怒火，所以这个词也用来形容周围人被它激怒的源头。

senses.title: To provoke by injustice
senses.definition: to make people angry by treating them unfairly or disregarding their rights
senses.definitionCN: 因对待不公或无视他人权利而使人愤怒
senses.example: The new tax infuriated small shop owners.
senses.exampleCN: 新税制把小店主们都气坏了。
senses.why: Rage is hottest when it follows a sense of injustice, so public anger often follows unfair rules.
senses.whyCN: 愤怒在不公之感之后燃得最猛，所以公众的愤怒常紧跟不公平的规则而来。

senses.title: To enrage in a public dispute
senses.definition: to drive a group into collective outrage during an argument or a campaign
senses.definitionCN: 在争论或活动之中把一群人推向集体愤怒
senses.example: The leaked recording infuriated both parties.
senses.exampleCN: 泄露的录音让双方都勃然大怒。
senses.why: The burning grows into a fire that spreads from one person to a crowd in a public quarrel.
senses.whyCN: 那点火会变成一把火，在公开争执中从一个人蔓延到一群人。

senses.title: To anger strongly without shouting
senses.definition: to make someone intensely angry while they keep the rage restrained
senses.definitionCN: 使人内心极度愤怒，却仍强忍着不外露
senses.example: Her calm reply infuriated him more than a shout would have.
senses.exampleCN: 她平静的回答比大喊更让他暴怒。
senses.why: Even a muted flame scorches, so the word can describe anger that burns inside a quiet person.
senses.whyCN: 再克制的外表也挡不住内里燃烧的火，所以这个词也能形容一位安静的人心中暗燃的怒火。

senses.title: Anger that looks fierce
senses.definition: showing an outward look of great anger through the face, voice, or gestures
senses.definitionCN: 通过表情、声音或动作流露出极度愤怒的样子
senses.example: An infuriated manager stormed out of the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 一位怒不可遏的经理冲出了会议室。
senses.why: The Latin root also carries the idea of frenzy, so the anger becomes visible as rushing out of the room.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根还带有「狂乱」的意味，于是愤怒外化为夺门而出。

senses.title: Prose that arouses anger
senses.definition: of writing or speech, to excite strong anger in the audience
senses.definitionCN: 就书面或口头表达而言，激起听众强烈的愤怒
senses.example: The editorial infuriated its opponents.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇社论激怒了它的反对者。
senses.why: Words carry the spark too, so a single editorial can set a whole readership alight.
senses.whyCN: 文字同样携带火星，一篇社论就能点燃整群读者。

intro.en: Infuriate comes from Latin in- plus the noun furia, rage, through the verb infuriare; the adjective and verb share the same root as fury and furious.
intro.cn: infuriate 经由拉丁语动词 infuriare 而来，由 in-（进入）加名词 furia（狂怒）构成，与 fury、furious 同源。

items.en: Furia means rage or frenzy, related to furere, to be mad.
items.cn: furia 意为狂怒、狂乱，与动词 furere（发狂）相关。

items.en: Infuriare adds in-, making someone enter a state of rage.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 infuriare 加上 in-，表示使人进入狂怒状态。

items.en: The verb passes into medieval and learned Latin usage.
items.cn: 这个动词进入中世纪及学术拉丁语的用法。

items.en: Infuriate first appears as a verb meaning to fill with rage.
items.cn: infuriate 在十六世纪先以动词形式出现，意为「使充满狂怒」。

items.en: The participle infuriated develops the adjective sense, more angry.
items.cn: 分词形式 infuriated 发展出形容词义「极其愤怒的」。

items.en: Infuriating settles as the common adjective for what provokes anger.
items.cn: 现代英语中 infuriating 固定为表示「令人愤怒的」常用形容词。

note.en: Infuriate sits with the fury family and with verbs of anger, from mild annoy to boiling outrage.
note.cn: infuriate 属于 fury 词族，也与表示激怒的动词相邻，从轻微的惹恼到暴怒的激怒。

normalIntro.en: Infuriate holds the rage noun furia inside, and the prefix in- drives that rage into someone.
normalIntro.cn: infuriate 里装着表狂怒的名词 furia，前缀 in- 把那股怒火推进某人心中。

normal.en: The infuriate family shares one root: fury, furious, infuriate, infuriating.
normal.cn: 这个家族共享一个词根：fury、furious、infuriate、infuriating。

normal.en: The prefix in- means into, so infuriate is literally to put rage into someone.
normal.cn: 前缀 in- 意为「进入」，因此 infuriate 字面上就是把怒火放进某人心里。

normal.en: Infuriate, enrage and provoke all take a person as the object after them.
normal.cn: infuriate、enrage、provoke 后面都可以接人作宾语。

normal.en: Keep infuriating apart from infuriatingly: the adverb marks degree in a comment.
normal.cn: 把 infuriating 与副词 infuriatingly 分开记：后者用于评论程度。

normal.en: Remember the -ate ending: it signals a verb, so you infuriate someone rather than infuriate at them.
normal.cn: 记住 -ate 结尾：它表示动词，所以你 infuriate someone，而不是加上介词 at。

abstract.cn: 想象一根火柴掉进干草堆，火苗一下子蹿起来。

abstract.en: Imagine a calm face turning red while the fists slowly close.
abstract.cn: 想象一张平静的脸慢慢涨红，拳头缓缓攥紧。

abstract.en: Think of a single careless sentence setting a whole room on fire.
abstract.cn: 想一想，一句不经意的话就能点燃整个屋子里的情绪。

examples.en: The constant delays infuriated the passengers.
examples.cn: 一再延误让乘客们愤怒不已。

examples.en: She was infuriated by the way her work was ignored.
examples.cn: 自己的工作被无视，这让她十分愤怒。

examples.en: Choosing a present became an infuriating task.
examples.cn: 挑选礼物竟成了一件令人恼火的事。

sensesIntro.en: Infuriate starts as the act of making someone furious, then spreads to the person who is furious, the thing that provokes anger, and public outrage.

branches.en: A quiet, restrained anger keeps the same inner fire.
branches.cn: 内敛的愤怒保留着同样的内火。

definition_zh: 注入；灌输；浸泡出味；充满（某物）
definition_en: to pour something in so that it spreads through, or to fill a person or thing with a quality
core_image: 热水缓缓倒进茶壶，茶香从叶片里一点点渗出来，浸满整壶水
scene: 老师把草本放进热水里，让香气慢慢渗出来，整杯茶都变得满室生香。The teacher let the herbs sit in hot water so that their flavour could infuse into the whole cup.
sceneCN: 这里 infuse 是「浸泡出味、渗入」（第 1 个义项：用浸泡让味道或成分进入液体）；句意：老师把草药放进热水里，让它们的味道渗进整杯茶。

derivatives.zh: 注入；浸剂；输液
可灌注的；可浸泡出味的
融合；熔合（同根名词）

senses.title: To steep and draw out flavour
senses.definition: to leave herbs or tea leaves in hot water so that their flavour and substances pass into it
senses.definitionCN: 把草药或茶叶留在热水中，使其味道和成分进入水里
senses.example: Let the herbs infuse for five minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 让草药浸泡五分钟，好让味道出来。
senses.why: The Latin verb infundere means to pour in, and steeping is pouring the plant contents into water drop by drop.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 infundere 意为「倒进」，冲泡就是把植物的成分一滴一滴倒入水中。

senses.title: To fill with a quality
senses.definition: to fill a person or thing with a feeling, quality, or energy that spreads through it
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或某物充满一种感受、品质或能量，并蔓延开来
senses.example: Her speech infused the team with confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 她的讲话给团队注入了信心。
senses.why: What is poured in spreads everywhere, so the pouring image becomes a picture of filling someone with a quality.
senses.whyCN: 倒进去的东西会四处扩散，于是「倒」的画面就变成了用某种品质充满一个人的比喻。

senses.title: To introduce an added element
senses.definition: to add something to a larger whole so that the whole takes on its character
senses.definitionCN: 把某物加入较大整体，使整体带上它的特性
senses.example: They infused the old building with modern light.
senses.exampleCN: 他们给这栋老建筑增添了现代的灯光。
senses.why: Any liquid poured into a larger container gives it colour and taste, so infuse names adding a new element to a whole.
senses.whyCN: 任何倒进大容器的液体都会给容器带来颜色和味道，于是 infuse 也指为整体增添新的元素。

senses.title: To spread through completely
senses.definition: of flavour, light, or feeling, to spread through a whole place or object until it is everywhere
senses.definitionCN: 指味道、光线或情绪在整个地方或物体中蔓延到无处不在
senses.example: Warm light infused the empty hall.
senses.exampleCN: 温暖的灯光弥漫了空荡的大厅。
senses.why: Once poured in, the liquid does not stay in one spot but seeps through the whole thing.
senses.whyCN: 倒进去的液体不会停在一处，而是渗过整个物体。

senses.title: To implant an idea
senses.definition: to pass an idea, belief, or habit into someone so that it becomes part of them
senses.definitionCN: 把观念、信念或习惯传进某人心里，使之成为其一部分
senses.example: The mentors infused a strong sense of duty in the young officers.
senses.exampleCN: 导师给年轻军官灌输了一种强烈的责任感。
senses.why: Ideas can be poured in just as liquid is, so teaching is pictured as a slow infusion of attitudes.
senses.whyCN: 观念也能像液体一样被倒进去，因此教育被想象成一点一点注入态度。

senses.title: To fill utterly
senses.definition: to make someone completely full of a particular feeling after the pouring has spread through them
senses.definitionCN: 在灌注蔓延之后让人心里满满都是某种感受
senses.example: He was infused with fresh hope after the news.
senses.exampleCN: 听到这个消息后，他心中充满了新的希望。
senses.why: When the liquid reaches every corner, the container itself takes on its quality, and a person can be filled in the same way.
senses.whyCN: 液体到达每个角落时，容器本身也带上了它的特性，人也能以同样方式被充满。

senses.title: To separate by drawing out
senses.definition: in science and pharmacy, to extract the soluble parts of a substance by soaking it in a liquid
senses.definitionCN: 在科学和药学中，通过把物质浸泡在液体里提取其可溶成分
senses.example: The active compounds were infused into the solvent.
senses.exampleCN: 有效成分被浸出到了溶剂中。
senses.why: The old pouring image survives in the laboratory, where the useful parts of a plant are poured out into a solvent.
senses.whyCN: 古老的「倒」意象在实验室中延续：植物的有用成分被倒出到溶剂里。

senses.title: To make tea by infusion
senses.definition: to prepare a hot drink by pouring water over tea leaves or herbs and letting them stand
senses.definitionCN: 把热水倒过茶叶或草药并静置，制成热饮
senses.example: She infused a pot of jasmine tea for the guests.
senses.exampleCN: 她给客人泡了一壶茉莉花茶。
senses.why: This is the most literal everyday act of pouring in, so infuse also names the making of a drink.
senses.whyCN: 这是「倒进」最朴素的日常动作，所以 infuse 也指制作饮品。

intro.en: Infuse comes from Latin infundere, to pour in, formed from in-, into, and fundere, to pour; the same root gives fusion and effuse.
intro.cn: infuse 源自拉丁语 infundere（倒进），由 in-（进入）与 fundere（倾倒）构成，同根词有 fusion、effuse。

items.en: Fundere means to pour, and in- means into.
items.cn: fundere 意为倾倒，in- 意为进入。

items.en: Infundere means to pour in or pour into.
items.cn: infundere 意为倒进、注入。

items.en: Learned Latin infusionem, a pouring in, enters French usage.
items.cn: 学术拉丁语 infusionem（倒入）进入法语。

items.en: Infuse arrives via French, first meaning to pour in liquid.
items.cn: infuse 经由法语进入英语，最初意为倒入液体。

items.en: The verb takes on the figurative sense of pouring in thoughts or feelings.
items.cn: 该动词获得比喻义，指注入思想或情感。

items.en: Modern English keeps tea infusing and ideals being infused into people.
items.cn: 现代英语既保留「泡茶出味」，也保留「把理念注入人心」。

note.en: Infuse belongs to the pouring family with fusion, effuse and confuse, and neighbours verbs of filling and adding.
note.cn: infuse 属于表示「倾倒」的词族，与 fusion、effuse、confuse 同根，并与表示「充满、添加」的动词相邻。

senses.title: Cleverness in solving problems
senses.definition: the power to think of clever and original ways of dealing with difficult problems
senses.definitionCN: 想出巧妙、独到的办法解决难题的能力
senses.example: The villagers solved the water shortage with simple ingenuity.
senses.exampleCN: 村民靠朴素的聪明才智解决了缺水问题。
senses.why: The Latin ingenium means native talent, so ingenuity names an inborn cleverness that meets a hard problem.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ingenium 意为天生的才能，于是 ingenuity 指面对难题时那种天生的机敏。

senses.title: A cleverly made device
senses.definition: an invention or method that is itself clever, surprising and well designed
senses.definitionCN: 本身就巧妙、出人意料而且设计精巧的发明或方法
senses.example: The free library is a piece of quiet ingenuity.
senses.exampleCN: 那个免费图书馆是个低调的巧思。
senses.why: The ability shows itself in things, so a gadget or scheme made with it is called ingenuity as well.
senses.whyCN: 这种能力会在物品上体现，因此用它做出的装置或办法也被称作 ingenuity。

senses.title: Originality in design
senses.definition: the quality of being original and inventive in how something is designed or arranged
senses.definitionCN: 某物的设计或布局富有原创性与发明性的特质
senses.example: Critics praised the ingenuity of the bridge design.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家称赞那座桥梁设计的独创性。
senses.why: Originality is the inborn cleverness of ingenium applied to shaping a structure.
senses.whyCN: 原创性就是 ingenium 那种天生机敏被用在塑造结构之上。

senses.title: Skill in practical tasks
senses.definition: skilful handling of tools or materials, especially in a workshop or craft
senses.definitionCN: 在工坊或手艺中灵巧地操作工具或材料
senses.example: The repair showed the plumber at his handiest and most inventive.
senses.exampleCN: 这次维修显示出水管工处理管道时手巧又富创意的那一面。
senses.why: Clever thinking at the workbench becomes skill in the hands, so ingenuity describes practical knack.
senses.whyCN: 工作台上的机敏思考会变成手上的技巧，因此 ingenuity 也指动手的诀窍。

senses.title: Resourcefulness under pressure
senses.definition: the ability to make good use of whatever is available when conditions are difficult
senses.definitionCN: 在条件艰难时善于利用手边一切资源的能力
senses.example: With little fuel, the pilots relied on sheer ingenuity.
senses.exampleCN: 燃料所剩无几，飞行员只能全靠急智。
senses.why: The talent grows when resources are scarce, so the word often describes making much of very little.
senses.whyCN: 资源匮乏时这种才能更显突出，所以这个词常形容用很少的东西做出很多。

senses.title: Inventive humour
senses.definition: an amusing cleverness that produces fresh and unexpected jokes or tricks
senses.definitionCN: 能制造新颖、出人意料的玩笑或把戏的机智
senses.example: Her speech was full of gentle ingenuity.
senses.exampleCN: 她的演讲洋溢着温和的机智。
senses.why: Originality in wit is the same talent turned to words, so a speaker can show ingenuity too.
senses.whyCN: 机智中的原创性与同一种才能转向言语时的表现相同，所以说话的人也能展现出 ingenuity。

senses.title: Collective inventiveness
senses.definition: the shared inventive power of a community, culture, or company over time
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体、文化或企业长期共享的发明创造能力
senses.example: Such cities thrive on the ingenuity of their people.
senses.exampleCN: 这样的城市靠人民的创造力兴旺发达。
senses.why: What one mind has can belong to a whole group, so people speak of the ingenuity of a nation or firm.
senses.whyCN: 一个人拥有的东西可以属于整个群体，于是人们说一个国家或公司的 ingenuity。

senses.title: Cleverness at tricking people
senses.definition: older or literary use, cleverness used to deceive or outwit others
senses.definitionCN: 较早或文学性的用法，指用于欺骗或胜过他人的机巧
senses.example: The plot turns on the low cunning that the merchant shows.
senses.exampleCN: 情节的转折全在于那个商人表现出的卑劣狡黠。
senses.why: The native cleverness of ingenium can serve deception as easily as it serves repair.
senses.whyCN: ingenium 那种天生机敏既能服务于修理，也同样能服务于欺骗。

intro.en: Ingenuity comes from Latin ingenuitas, the condition of a free man, from ingenuus, free-born, and ingenium, inborn talent; the noun kept the talent sense, while the related adjective is now commonly ingenious.
intro.cn: ingenuity 源自拉丁语 ingenuitas（自由民身份），来自 ingenuus（生而自由）与 ingenium（天赋）；该词保留的是「天赋」义，其形容词常用形式是 ingenious。

items.en: Gignere means to beget, and in- adds the idea of something inborn.
items.cn: gignere 意为生育，in- 加上「与生俱来」的意味。

items.en: Ingenium means natural talent or cleverness, and ingenuus means free-born.
items.cn: ingenium 意为天赋、机敏，ingenuus 意为生而自由的。

items.en: Ingenuitas names the rank of a free man as well as frankness.
items.cn: ingenuitas 既指自由民的身份，也指坦率。

items.en: Ingenuity arrives meaning noble birth or frankness.
items.cn: ingenuity 进入英语时意为高贵出身或坦率。

items.en: The sense shifts to natural cleverness and inventive skill.
items.cn: 词义转向天生的机敏与发明才能。

items.en: The noun is now tied to ingenious and to clever devices and designs.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个名词与 ingenious 以及巧妙的装置设计紧密关联。

note.en: Ingenuity pairs with ingenious in the same family and sits next to words for creativity and inventiveness.
note.cn: ingenuity 与同族形容词 ingenious 成对使用，并与表示创造力、发明才能的词相邻。

innocent and frank

normalIntro.en: Ingenuity and its adjective ingenious both carry ingenium, the Latin gift of inborn talent.
normalIntro.cn: ingenuity 与其形容词 ingenious 都带着 ingenium，即拉丁语中「天生才能」的馈赠。

normal.en: Ingenuity is the noun, and ingenious is the adjective you pair with it.
normal.cn: ingenuity 是名词，与它搭配的形容词是 ingenious。

normal.en: The word begins with in-gen, echoing inborn, the talent you are born with.
normal.cn: 这个词以 in-gen 开头，呼应「与生俱来」，也就是天生拥有的才能。

normal.en: Keep it apart from ingenue and ingenuous: ingenuous means innocent, not clever.
normal.cn: 要把 ingenuity 与拼写相近的 ingenuous 分开：后者意为天真，不是聪明。

normal.en: Human ingenuity is a common phrase in essays about technology and survival.
normal.cn: human ingenuity 是科技与生存类作文里的常见短语。

normal.en: Ingenuity takes no article when it is the abstract quality, so say with great ingenuity.
normal.cn: 表示抽象品质时，ingenuity 不加冠词，所以说 with great ingenuity。

abstract.en: Picture a child turning a broken radio into a lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子把坏掉的收音机改造成一盏灯。

abstract.en: Imagine a crowd of engineers sketching a bridge with no straight lines.
abstract.cn: 想象一群工程师画出一座没有一条直线的桥。

abstract.en: Think of someone inventing a tool from a spoon and a rubber band.
abstract.cn: 想一想有人用一把勺子和一根橡皮筋发明出一件工具。

examples.en: The invention is a monument to human ingenuity.
examples.cn: 这项发明是人类智慧的丰碑。

examples.en: Solving the puzzle took patience and ingenuity.
examples.cn: 解开这个谜题既需要耐心，也需要机敏。

examples.en: Engineers admired the ingenuity of the folding chair.
examples.cn: 工程师们赞叹那把折叠椅设计之巧妙。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「in + genie + ous」——像一个精灵藏在你脑子里，随手就能想出巧办法；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 gignere（生育）→ in- + genium → ingenuus（生而自由的）与 ingenium（天赋）→ ingenuitas（自由民身份）→ 古法语 → 英语 ingenuity；同源形容词为 ingenious。

sensesIntro.en: Ingenuity begins as the inborn talent for finding clever solutions, then refers to the clever things made with it, to design and hand skill, and to wit and even cunning.
sensesIntro.cn: ingenuity 先指「想出巧妙办法的天生才能」，再指用它做出的巧妙之物，以及设计与手上功夫、机智乃至狡黠。

core.cn: 核心意象：桌上散落的零件忽然被拼成一台能用的机器。

branches.en: The core sense is the native power to solve problems cleverly.
branches.cn: 核心义项是巧妙解决问题的天赋能力。

branches.en: The talent becomes visible in clever devices and original designs.
branches.cn: 这种才能在巧妙的装置与原创设计中显露出来。

branches.en: At the workbench, cleverness becomes skill in the hands.
branches.cn: 在工作台上，机敏变成手上的巧劲。

branches.en: Under pressure and in groups the talent is tested and shared.
branches.cn: 在压力之下和群体之中，这种才能受到考验并被共享。

branches.en: The same cleverness can turn to wit, or to cunning.
branches.cn: 同一种机敏可以转向机智，也可以转向狡黠。

intro.en: Ingenuity is built on the Latin stem gen-, inborn, with the noun suffix -ity; English pairs it with ingenious and ingeniously.
intro.cn: ingenuity 建立在拉丁语词干 gen-（生来）与名词后缀 -ity 之上，英语中与 ingenious、ingeniously 成对出现。

latinIntro.en: Latin ingenium means inborn talent, ingenuus means free-born, and ingenuitas means frankness or free birth.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ingenium 意为天赋，ingenuus 意为生而自由的，ingenuitas 意为坦率或自由民出身。

items.example: The prefix in- marks something within a person.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 标示存在于人自身之内的东西。

items.example: The root gen- links birth to natural talent.
items.exampleCN: 词根 gen- 把出生与天赋联系起来。

items.example: Ingenium is the talent inside the word.

items.example: Ingenuus gives both clever and innocent descendants.
items.exampleCN: ingenuus 同时衍生出「聪明」与「天真」两类词。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的词尾

items.exampleCN: ingenious 描述巧妙的装置或人。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms ingeniously.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 ingeniously。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms ingeniousness.

senses.title: Innocent and frank
senses.definition: honest and straightforward in a way that shows no hidden motive
senses.definitionCN: 真诚直率、看不出隐藏动机的天真坦率
senses.example: Her ingenuous smile made everyone in the room relax.
senses.exampleCN: 她天真的微笑让屋里所有人都放松下来。
senses.why: Latin ingenuus meant native and freeborn, so the core image is a person with nothing to hide behind a mask.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ingenuus 意为「本地的、生来自由的」，所以核心画面是一个无需躲在面具后面的人。

senses.title: Without worldly experience
senses.titleCN: 不知世故的；单纯无城府
senses.definition: lacking experience of the world and therefore easily deceived
senses.definitionCN: 缺少世事经验，因而容易被蒙骗的单纯
senses.example: The villagers were so ingenuous that they trusted every stranger.
senses.exampleCN: 村民们太不知世故，对每个外人都毫不怀疑。
senses.why: A freeborn citizen was not a trained negotiator; the same root later came to label naive openness.
senses.whyCN: 生来自由的平民并非久经训练的谈判者，同一词根后来就用来表示这种「不设防的直白」。

senses.title: Natural and unaffected
senses.definition: simple and natural, with no artificial polish
senses.definitionCN: 朴素自然、没有人工雕琢感的
senses.example: The actor kept a surprisingly ingenuous style despite his fame.
senses.exampleCN: 这位演员尽管出名，仍保持着令人意外的质朴风格。
senses.why: What is inborn is unpolished, so ingenuous can praise plainness in art or manners.
senses.whyCN: 「生来就有的东西」不经打磨，于是 ingenuous 也可以用来称赞艺术家或谈吐的朴素。

senses.title: In art: unposed realism
senses.titleCN: 艺术上：不加修饰的自然
senses.definition: in art or writing, presenting life plainly without ironic distance
senses.definitionCN: 在艺术或写作中平实呈现生活，不带反讽的距离感
senses.example: The early paintings have an ingenuous charm that critics later missed.
senses.exampleCN: 这些早期画作带着一种天真的魅力，批评家后来再也找不到。
senses.why: From freeborn simplicity comes a style praised for its lack of pretence rather than its skill.
senses.whyCN: 由「生来的质朴」延伸出一种以不做作而非技巧取胜的风格。

senses.title: Sincerely open in speech
senses.definition: speaking with sincere openness, sometimes awkwardly so
senses.definitionCN: 说话真心毫无防备，有时甚至显得笨拙
senses.example: He was too ingenuous to notice that his joke had upset her.
senses.exampleCN: 他太不设防，竟没察觉自己的玩笑冒犯了对方。
senses.why: Because nothing is hidden, the word often carries a trace of awkwardness in social situations.
senses.whyCN: 正因为什么都不藏，这个词在社交场合常带一点笨拙的意味。

intro.en: Ingenuous comes from Latin ingenuus, meaning native or freeborn, built on gignere, to beget, so the root idea is a person who is born that way.
intro.cn: ingenuous 经古法语进入英语，源自拉丁语 ingenuus（本地的、生来自由的），其根 gignere 意为「生育」，所以本义是「生来就是」这一层意思。

items.en: The Latin root gignere means to beget or bring forth.
items.cn: 拉丁词根 gignere 意为生育、产生。

items.en: Ingenuus means inborn and freeborn, as opposed to a freed slave.
items.cn: ingenuus 意为「生来的、天生自由的」，与获得自由的奴隶相对。

items.en: Cicero and others use ingenuus for natural candour in character and speech.
items.cn: 西塞罗等人用 ingenuus 表示性格与言辞中的天然坦率。

items.en: Scholars think French jeune (young) descends from Latin iuvenis, which belongs to a different root, and the classic warning about false friends is often traced to a saying attributed to Saint Augustine.
items.cn: 一般认为法语 jeune（年轻的）来自拉丁语 iuvenis，属于另一词根；而「貌似之友误人」的提醒通常追溯到圣奥古斯丁的一句拉丁语。

items.en: English adopts ingenuous meaning frank and free from deceit.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪吸收 ingenuous，义为「坦率的、不欺瞒的」。

items.en: The sense of innocent simplicity shades into naive in later use.
items.cn: 「单纯无知」的一面在后来的使用中逐渐偏向「幼稚」。

note.en: Ingenuous belongs to the freeborn family, easily confused with ingenious and with ingenuity; its near meanings are candid, naive, and artless.
note.cn: ingenuous 属于表示「生来自由」的词族，容易与 ingenious、ingenuity 混淆；它的近义是坦白、幼稚与不做作。

honest and direct in what one says
