normalIntro.en: Ingenuous is the freeborn adjective: a person born with nothing to hide, so they simply say what they mean.
normalIntro.cn: ingenuous 是「生来自由」的形容词：一个生来就没什么好遮掩的人，因此他想到什么就说什么。

normal.en: Ingenuous shares the in- and genu- shape with genuine: what is genuine is not disguised, and what is ingenuous does not pretend.
normal.cn: ingenuous 与 genuine 共享 in- 与 genu- 的外形：genuine 的东西不掺假，ingenuous 的人不装假。

normal.en: The negative form disingenuous means pretending to be frank, so the base word must mean truly frank.
normal.cn: 它的否定形式 disingenuous 表示假装坦率，可见基础词的意思正是真心坦率。

normal.en: Keep ingenuous apart from ingenious: a clever engineer is ingenious, an open heart is ingenuous.
normal.cn: 把 ingenuous 与 ingenious 分开记：聪明的工程师是 ingenious，敞亮的心才是 ingenuous。

normal.en: Ingenuity looks related but means cleverness, so a common use in TOEFL tests is a trap in spelling only.
normal.cn: ingenuity 看起来同源，实际指机灵，所以在托福考试里常只是一个拼写陷阱。

normal.en: The adverb ingenuously signals that the frankness is whole, as in she answered ingenuously.
normal.cn: 副词 ingenuously 强调坦率完全是出于本心，如 she answered ingenuously 一句。

abstract.en: Picture a child holding out both palms and offering whatever is inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子摊开两只手掌，把掌心里的东西直接递给你。

abstract.en: Imagine a door that has no lock because the owner trusts everyone who knocks.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇没有锁的门，因为屋主信任每一个敲门的人。

abstract.en: Picture a clear spring: you can see the pebbles at the bottom, nothing hides in the water.
abstract.cn: 想象一汪清澈的泉：底下的石子看得一清二楚，水里藏不住任何东西。

examples.en: She asked an ingenuous question that no one else dared to raise.
examples.cn: 她问了一个天真的问题，别人都不敢提。

examples.en: His ingenuous manner hides a sharp and careful mind.
examples.cn: 他天真的举止掩盖着一颗敏锐而缜密的心。

examples.en: The novel is written in an ingenuous voice that never mocks its characters.
examples.cn: 这部小说用一种朴素的笔调写成，从不嘲弄自己的角色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬 genu 硬」——把「真」字硬邦邦地摆出来，不拐弯也不改装，就记住了「天真坦率」；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 gignere（生育）→ 形容词 ingenuus（生来的、生来自由的）→ 古法语 → 英语 ingenuous，核心义「生来是什么样就露出什么样」。

sensesIntro.en: Ingenuous starts from a face with nothing to hide, extends to a person without worldly training, and then to art and speech that refuse polish.
sensesIntro.cn: ingenuous 从一张没什么可隐藏的脸出发，延伸到不谙世事的人，再延伸到拒绝修饰的艺术与言语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open palm showing everything it holds.
core.cn: 核心意象：摊开的手掌，掌心里的东西一览无余。

branches.en: Frank openness is the central everyday sense.
branches.cn: 坦率开放是日常使用的中心义项。

branches.en: Missing worldly training is the cost of that openness.
branches.cn: 缺少世事历练是这份坦率的代价。

branches.en: Plainness in style grows out of unattended nature.
branches.cn: 风格上的朴素由「未经雕琢的天性」长出来。

branches.en: An ingenuous person is frank and also easily deceived.
branches.cn: 天真坦率的人既真心，也容易受骗。

branches.en: Both unposed art and awkward speech keep the same refusal to perform.
branches.cn: 不加修饰的艺术与笨拙的直言都保留了「不做表演」的内核。

intro.en: Ingenuous is built on the Latin root gen- with the freeborn adjective ingenuus, and English grows ingenuously, ingenuousness, and disingenuous from it.
intro.cn: ingenuous 建在拉丁词根 gen- 之上，来自「生来自由」的形容词 ingenuus，英语再从中长出 ingenuously、ingenuousness 与 disingenuous。

latinIntro.en: Latin gignere means to beget, and ingenitus means inborn, so the freeborn adjective is there from the start.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 gignere 意为生育，ingenitus 意为生来的，所以「生来自由」的形容词义从一开始就存在。

items.meaning: to beget, to come into being
items.example: The root gen- sits inside ingenuous and genuine.
items.exampleCN: 词根 gen- 出现在 ingenuous 与 genuine 之中。

items.example: Gignere is the parent verb of the root.
items.exampleCN: gignere 是该词根的源头动词。

items.example: Ingenitus keeps the sense of what is born in us.
items.exampleCN: ingenitus 保留了「与生俱来」的意思。

items.meaningCN: 生来自由的；天然的；坦率的
items.example: Ingenuus is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: ingenuus 是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: Ingenuous names the frank quality.
items.exampleCN: ingenuous 指天真坦率的品质。

items.example: The suffix -ous makes an adjective of the stem.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 把词干变成形容词。

items.example: The adverb ingenuously describes how one speaks.
items.exampleCN: 副词 ingenuously 描述说话的方式。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ness forms the noun ingenuousness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成名词 ingenuousness。

items.example: The prefix dis- reverses the frankness.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 dis- 把坦率反转过来。

items.example: Ingenuity looks like a relative but means cleverness.
items.exampleCN: ingenuity 看似同族，实际指机灵。

definition_zh: 吸入；吸气；吸（烟）
definition_en: to draw air, a gas, or smoke into the lungs through the nose or mouth
core_image: 胸腔像风箱一样向外撑开，把外面的空气吸进来
scene: 潜水员浮出水面后，先大口吸一口气，再向同伴打手势。The diver surfaced and inhaled deeply before signalling to the boat.
sceneCN: 这里 inhale 是「吸气」（第 2 个义项：把空气吸入肺里）；句意：潜水员浮出水面，深吸一口气，然后向船上打手势。

derivatives.zh: 吸入；吸气；吸入物
吸入器（哮喘病人用的喷雾装置）
由同一拉丁词根加相反前缀构成，义为「呼出；呼气」

senses.title: To breathe in air
senses.definition: to take air into the lungs through the nose or mouth
senses.definitionCN: 经鼻子或嘴把空气吸入肺里
senses.example: The doctor told her to inhale slowly and then hold her breath.
senses.exampleCN: 医生让她慢慢吸气，然后屏住呼吸。
senses.why: Latin halare means to breathe, and the prefix in- means into, so the word simply places the breath inside.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 halare 意为呼吸，前缀 in- 表示「向内」，所以这个词就是把气息放进身体里。

senses.title: To take a substance into the lungs
senses.definition: to draw a gas, vapour, smoke, or dust into the body through breathing
senses.definitionCN: 通过呼吸把气体、蒸气、烟雾或粉尘吸进体内
senses.example: Workers who inhale silica dust may develop serious lung disease.
senses.exampleCN: 吸入硅尘的工人可能患上严重的肺病。
senses.why: Once the breath goes inside, anything carried with it goes inside too, so inhale becomes the verb for harm from the air.
senses.whyCN: 气息一旦进入身体，随它一起的东西也一并进入，于是 inhale 成了描述空气危害的动词。

senses.title: To breathe in smoke deliberately
senses.definition: to draw cigarette or pipe smoke down into the lungs on purpose
senses.definitionCN: 有意把香烟或烟斗的烟吸入肺中
senses.example: Fewer young smokers now inhale when they light a cigarette.
senses.exampleCN: 如今尝试吸烟的年轻人中，把烟吸入肺里的更少了。
senses.why: The medical sense of moving air inward is applied to smoke, and smoking culture turns it into a deliberate act.
senses.whyCN: 把空气向内推进的医学义被套用到烟雾上，吸烟习惯再让它成为一种有意的动作。

senses.title: To absorb eagerly
senses.definition: figurative use for taking in praise, ideas, or atmosphere eagerly
senses.definitionCN: 比喻义：急切地把赞美、观念或气氛吸纳进来
senses.example: The audience seemed to inhale every word of the speech.
senses.exampleCN: 听众仿佛把演讲的每个字都吸了进去。
senses.why: The physical pull of breath inwards gives a vivid image for absorbing something with delight.
senses.whyCN: 吸气的物理动作提供了一个鲜明画面，用来形容满心欢喜地吸收某物。

senses.title: In yoga and sports: controlled intake
senses.titleCN: 瑜伽与运动中：有控制地吸气
senses.definition: in exercise, to time the breath so that the body expands on the inward breath
senses.definitionCN: 在运动中让身体随吸气扩张、按节奏控制呼吸
senses.example: Inhale as you raise your arms, then exhale as you lower them.
senses.exampleCN: 抬臂时吸气，放下时呼气。
senses.why: Because halare marks the breath itself, the verb becomes a technical instruction in breathing technique.
senses.whyCN: halare 标记的是「呼吸」本身，所以这个动词也成了呼吸技巧中的技术指令。

intro.en: Inhale joins Latin in-, meaning into, with halare, meaning to breathe, and the pair arrive in English in the early modern period, balanced by exhale.
intro.cn: inhale 由拉丁语 in-（向内）与 halare（呼吸）结合而成，在近代早期与 exhale 一起进入英语。

items.en: Halare means to breathe or to give off breath or vapour.
items.cn: halare 意为呼吸，或散出气息、蒸气。

items.en: The prefix in- means into or towards, so in plus halare is to breathe in.
items.cn: 前缀 in- 表示「进入、朝向」，所以 in 加 halare 就是「向内呼吸」。

items.en: Related halitus names a breath or vapour, and the same root yields exhalare, to breathe out.
items.cn: 同族的 halitus 指气息或蒸气，同一词根也生出 exhale（呼出）。

items.en: Medical and scientific writing of the early modern period adopts inhale for taking air or vapour into the lungs.
items.cn: 近代早期的医学和科学写作吸收了 inhale，用来表示把空气或蒸气吸入肺里。

items.en: With the spread of smoking culture, inhale comes to mean drawing smoke into the lungs.
items.cn: 随着吸烟文化的普及，inhale 又获得「把烟吸进肺里」的意思。

items.en: Modern usage adds figurative ideas of absorbing praise or atmosphere eagerly.
items.cn: 现代用法又增添了「急切吸收赞美或气氛」的比喻义。

note.en: Inhale is the inward member of the halare breath pair, easily confused with inhale-shaped words and with the everyday verb breathe.
note.cn: inhale 是 halare 词族中表示「向内」的一方，既容易与外形相近的词混淆，也容易和日常词 breathe 混用。

entries.definition: to breathe out
the act of breathing something in
a device that delivers medicine into the lungs
the everyday general verb for taking air in and out
to draw breath in, now mostly figurative as to stir up ideas
entries.definitionCN: （书面）吸气；现今多作比喻，指激发

entries.definition: to draw air in sharply through the nose

normalIntro.en: Inhale is the breathing-in verb: in- marks the direction, and halare marks the breath, so the word is a breath going inside.
normalIntro.cn: inhale 是「吸气」动词：in- 标记方向，halare 标记呼吸，整个词就是一口向内走的气息。

normal.en: Memorise the pair inhale and exhale: the first prefix pushes in, the second pushes out.
normal.cn: 把 inhale 与 exhale 成对记：前者的前缀向内推，后者的前缀向外送。

normal.en: Inhalation and inhaler both keep the action of drawing something into the lungs.
normal.cn: inhalation 与 inhaler 都保留了「把东西吸进肺里」的动作。

normal.en: Medical labels such as the inhaler for asthma anchor the word in a scene you can picture.
normal.cn: 哮喘病人用的 inhaler 这类医学标签，把词固定在可想象的场景里。

normal.en: Do not mix it up with inhale as a spelling of inhale: obey the single h after in.
normal.cn: 不要把它和 inhale 的错拼混淆：in 之后只写一个 h。

normal.en: The verb pairs naturally with deeply, smoke, and fumes, so learn inhale deeply as a unit.
normal.cn: 这个动词常与 deeply、smoke、fumes 搭配，把 inhale deeply 当成整体来记。

abstract.en: Picture a bellows opening wide and pulling air through a small valve.
abstract.cn: 想象风箱张开，从小阀门里把空气抽进去。

abstract.en: Imagine a straw in a glass of water: the liquid climbs up as you pull.
abstract.cn: 想象吸管插在水杯里，你一吸，水就顺着管子往上爬。

abstract.en: Think of fog sliding into an empty room through a window left open.
abstract.cn: 想象雾从半开的窗子滑进一间空屋。

examples.en: She inhaled the cold morning air and felt awake at once.
examples.cn: 她吸入清冷的晨间空气，立刻清醒了。

examples.en: Passengers were warned not to inhale fumes from the fire.
examples.cn: 乘客被告知不要吸入火场的烟雾。

examples.en: Inhalation of fine dust can damage the lungs over many years.
examples.cn: 长期吸入细粉尘会损伤肺部。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因黑尔」——因为有灰尘太黑，只好先深吸一口气再进屋；这里的「吸」就是 inhale，只是中文谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（向内）+ halare（呼吸）→ 近代英语 inhale「吸气」，与 exhale、inhalation、inhaler 同族，核心义「把气息收进身体」。

sensesIntro.en: Inhale begins with the plain act of drawing breath in, extends to drawing harmful vapour or smoke down, and finally becomes a figure for absorbing anything greedily.
sensesIntro.cn: inhale 从最朴素的「吸一口气」开始，延伸到把有害气体或烟雾吸下去，最后成为「如饥似渴地吸收」的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the chest opening like a bellows and pulling air inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：胸腔像风箱一样张开，把空气拉进体内。

branches.en: The simple inward breath is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 最简单的吸气是日常义项。

branches.en: Anything carried by the inward breath enters too.
branches.cn: 随吸气而来的东西也一并进入。

branches.en: Smoke is the specific substance inhaled on purpose.
branches.cn: 烟雾是被人有意吸入的特定物质。

branches.en: Controlled breathing calls the same act a technique.
branches.cn: 有控制的呼吸给同一动作起了技术上的名称。

branches.en: Absorbing praise echoes the pull of taking vapour in.
branches.cn: 吸收赞美沿用了吸入气体的拉力意象。

intro.en: Inhale pairs the Latin prefix in- with the breath root hal-, and English builds inhalation, inhaler, and the opposite exhale around it.
intro.cn: inhale 把拉丁语前缀 in- 与呼吸词根 hal- 配在一起，英语再围绕它构成 inhalation、inhaler 与反义的 exhale。

latinIntro.en: Latin halare means to breathe, and in with halare gives a verb for breathing air into the lungs.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 halare 意为呼吸，in 与 halare 合起来就是「把空气吸进肺里」的动词。

items.example: The prefix in- points the action inwards.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 把动作指向内部。

items.example: The root hal- carries the breath.
items.exampleCN: 词根 hal- 承载「呼吸」之义。

items.meaning: to breathe, to give off vapour
items.example: Halare is the direct parent verb.
items.exampleCN: halare 是直接的源头动词。

items.example: Halitus names the puff of breath itself.
items.exampleCN: halitus 指呼出的一口气本身。

items.example: Inhale names the inward act.
items.exampleCN: inhale 指吸入的动作。

items.meaningCN: 表示过程或动作的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ation forms inhalation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 inhalation。

items.example: Inhalation is the noun of the process.
items.exampleCN: inhalation 是表示该过程的名词。

items.meaningCN: 表示做某事的工具或人的词尾
items.example: The suffix -er forms inhaler, a device.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成表示器具的 inhaler。

items.example: An inhaler sends medicine straight to the lungs.
items.exampleCN: inhaler 把药直接送进肺里。

items.example: The prefix ex- reverses the inward motion.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ex- 把向内的动作反转过来。

items.example: Exhalare is the twin verb with the opposite prefix.
items.exampleCN: exhalare 是带相反前缀的孪生动词。

definition_zh: 不好客的；冷淡的；不宜居住的；（土地、气候）严酷荒凉的
definition_en: unfriendly to guests, or harsh and difficult for people to live in
core_image: 一扇本该为客人打开的门死死关着，门外只剩风声
scene: 荒野徒步者走了很久，眼前没有村镇，也找不到可以借宿的房子。They walked for hours across an inhospitable plain where no village offered food or shelter.
sceneCN: 这里 inhospitable 是「（地方）不宜居住的；严酷的」（第 2 个义项：环境恶劣，不适合人居住或通行）；句意：他们在荒凉的原野上走了几个小时，没有任何村庄提供食物或住处。

derivatives.zh: 不友好（尤指对客人）；冷淡
去掉否定前缀后的基础词，义为「好客的；宜人的」
与基础词同族的名词，义为「好客；殷勤款待」

senses.title: Unfriendly to guests
senses.definition: not welcoming to guests or visitors
senses.definitionCN: 对客人或来访者不热情的
senses.example: The village was inhospitable, and every door stayed shut.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村庄不好客，每一扇门都紧闭着。
senses.why: Latin hospes names both a host and a guest, and the prefix in- denies the welcome, so the word is the exact refusal of hospitality.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 hospes 既指主人也指客人，前缀 in- 否定了这份欢迎，所以这个词正是「不接待」的精确说法。

senses.title: Harsh and hard to live in
senses.definition: of a place or climate, offering little food, water, or comfort
senses.definitionCN: 形容地方或气候缺少食物、水和舒适条件
senses.example: Only a few species survive in that inhospitable desert.
senses.exampleCN: 只有少数物种能在那片不宜居住的沙漠中存活下来。
senses.why: A land that gives no welcome to people repeats the same refusal toward guests, only now the guest is a whole human community.
senses.whyCN: 一片不欢迎人的土地，重复了面对客人时的那种拒绝，只是这里的「客人」变成了整个人类社群。

senses.title: Hostile in attitude
senses.titleCN: 态度上冷冰冰的；不友好
senses.definition: showing coldness or hostility in manner rather than in action
senses.definitionCN: 举止上冷淡或敌意，而不是做出实际伤害
senses.example: Her inhospitable tone made it clear the interview was over.
senses.exampleCN: 她冷淡的语气明说面试已经结束。
senses.why: The word keeps the social image of a shut door and applies it to a face or a voice.
senses.whyCN: 这个词保留「关门」的社交画面，再把它用到一张脸或一个声音上。

senses.title: Poor for plant or animal life
senses.definition: in science, describing soil, water, or habitat poorly suited to living things
senses.definitionCN: 科学语境中描述不适合生物生长的土壤、水体或栖息地
senses.example: Coral reefs are increasingly inhospitable to young fish.
senses.exampleCN: 珊瑚礁对幼鱼来说越来越不宜栖息。
senses.why: Scientific writing borrows the everyday sense of an unwelcoming place for habitats that give no welcome to living things.
senses.whyCN: 科学写作借用了「地方不欢迎人」的日常义，用来描述不欢迎生物的栖息地。

senses.title: Lacking welcome in literature
senses.definition: in creative writing, a setting or house that seems to reject the people inside it
senses.definitionCN: 在文学创作中，指仿佛排斥其中人物的场景或房屋
senses.example: The house in the novel is inhospitable, dark, and full of locked rooms.
senses.exampleCN: 小说里的房子毫无暖意，幽暗，满是锁着的房间。
senses.why: A setting made of locked rooms turns hospitality into a visible absence, which is what the word shows in fiction.
senses.whyCN: 由锁着的房间构成的场景，把「好客」变成一种可见的缺席，这正是这个词在小说里呈现的样貌。

intro.en: Inhospitable is the negative form of hospitable, which come from Latin hospes, a host or guest, itself based on the root seen in hospitium, hospitality.
intro.cn: inhospitable 是 hospitable 的否定形式，二者都源于拉丁语 hospes（主人或客人），而 hospes 基于 hospitium（好客、寄宿）一词的词根。

items.en: Hospes means both host and guest, since the two roles share one bond of welcome.
items.cn: hospes 既指主人也指客人，因为这两个角色共享同一份欢迎的义务。

items.en: Hospitium means hospitality, a guest room, and the tie between host and guest.
items.cn: hospitium 意为好客、客房，以及主客之间的义务关系。

items.en: Scholars connect these words with a presumed root of proto-italic origin; the widely repeated tie to a Latin word for stranger is a later conjecture.
items.cn: 一般认为这些词来自一个原始意大利语系的假定词根；把它与拉丁语中表示「陌生人」的词联系起来的说法，是较晚的推测。

items.en: French hospitable carries the word toward English, through forms such as hospice and hospitality.
items.cn: 法语的 hospitable 把这个词带向英语，途中也经过 hospice、hospitality 等形式。

items.en: English records inhospitable in the late sixteenth century for persons and places alike.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪后期记录了 inhospitable，人与地方都可描述。

items.en: Modern science uses the word for planets, deserts, and habitats.
items.cn: 现代科学把这个词用于行星、沙漠与栖息地。

note.en: Inhospitable is the refused welcome: a near twin of hospitable and hospitality, and a close neighbour of hostile, barren, and bleak.
note.cn: inhospitable 是一份被拒绝的欢迎：它与 hospitable、hospitality 是近似孪生词，与 hostile、barren、bleak 意义相邻。

entries.definition: friendly to guests
the friendly treatment of guests
a place of care; it once sheltered guests and the sick and shares the welcome root
entries.definitionCN: 医院；最初是收留客人、病者的庇护所

entries.definition: unfriendly and ready to oppose
unable to support plants or life
lacking comfort, shelter, or hope
entries.definitionCN: 荒凉的；无遮蔽的；惨淡的

normalIntro.en: Inhospitable is hospitality with a door slammed shut: the prefix denies the welcome that the hospes root gives guests.
normalIntro.cn: inhospitable 是关上门的好客：前缀否定了 hospes 词根本应给客人的那份欢迎。

normal.en: Drop the in- and you get hospitable, so the word means the opposite of a welcome.
normal.cn: 去掉前缀 in- 就得到 hospitable，所以这个词的意思正是欢迎的反面。

normal.en: Hospitality and hospital share the same root: both once welcomed people who needed a room.
normal.cn: hospitality 与 hospital 同根：两者本来都用于接待需要一间房的人。

normal.en: The word serves two settings, people and places, so an inhospitable person and an inhospitable coast use one image.
normal.cn: 这个词兼用于人与地方，因此「冷淡的人」与「荒凉的海岸」用的是同一个画面。

normal.en: Biology uses it for habitats, so an inhospitable reef offers no welcome to young fish.
normal.cn: 生物学用它描述栖息地，所以说 not welcoming 的礁石对幼鱼毫无欢迎之意。

normal.en: The adverb inhospitably and noun inhospitality keep the shut door in view.
normal.cn: 副词 inhospitably 与名词 inhospitality 都保留了那扇关着的门。

abstract.en: Picture a guest knocking, and the door chain sliding across the gap.
abstract.cn: 想象客人敲门，门链却在门缝上一格一格地拉过去。

abstract.en: Imagine a beach of salt flats with no shade and no water for miles around.
abstract.cn: 想象一片盐碱滩，周围几十里都没有荫凉，也没有水。

abstract.en: Think of a sign on a fence reading closed to visitors, even though the gate is open.
abstract.cn: 想象栅栏上挂着一块「谢绝访客」的牌子，尽管大门开着。

examples.en: Local families were kind, but the inn staff were oddly inhospitable.
examples.cn: 当地人很友善，可这家旅店的服务员却出奇地冷淡。

examples.en: Few crops can grow in such an inhospitable climate.
examples.cn: 在如此严酷的气候里，很少有作物能生长。

examples.en: The planetary probe found an inhospitable surface of rock and ice.
examples.cn: 这颗行星探测器发现了一片由岩石和冰构成的严酷地表。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬是皮太薄」——硬邦邦的皮太薄，客人一来就沉下脸；这只是中文谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 hospes（主人、客人）+ hospitium（好客、寄宿）→ 拉丁语 hospitale → 英语 hospitable → 加否定前缀 in- 得 inhospitable，核心义「拒绝收留」。

sensesIntro.en: Inhospitable begins with a person who will not take in a guest, moves to a land that will not take in a traveler, and then widens to faces, attitudes, and habitats.
sensesIntro.cn: inhospitable 从「不愿收留客人的人」开始，转到「不愿收留旅人的土地」，再扩展到表情、态度与栖息地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door that should open for a guest stays shut and bolted.
core.cn: 核心意象：本该为客人打开的门，反而死死关上并插上门闩。

branches.en: Refusing welcome to a person is the social sense.
branches.cn: 拒绝欢迎来客是社交层面的义项。

branches.en: A place that refuses welcome is the environmental sense.
branches.cn: 拒绝欢迎来客的地方是环境层面的义项。

branches.en: The shut door on a face is the attitude sense.
branches.cn: 把紧闭的门放到了脸上，就是态度义项。

branches.en: Both a harsh coast and a poor habitat refuse what new life needs.
branches.cn: 荒凉的海岸与贫乏的栖息地都拒绝新生命所需的条件。

branches.en: Manners and words can be as closed as a locked gate.
branches.cn: 举止与言辞可以像锁上的大门一样紧闭。

intro.en: Inhospitable wraps the Russian-style negation in- around the hospitality word hospitable, and English adds inhospitality, inhospitably, and the base forms hospital and hospitality.
intro.cn: inhospitable 用否定前缀 in- 包裹住表示好客的 hospitable，英语再衍生出 inhospitality、inhospitably，以及基础词 hospital 与 hospitality。

latinIntro.en: Latin hospes means host and guest alike, and hospitium means hospitality, the source of the whole welcome family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 hospes 兼指主人与客人，hospitium 意为好客，是整个「欢迎」词族的源头。

items.example: The prefix in- turns hospitable into its opposite.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 把 hospitable 变成反义词。

items.example: Hospes covers both sides of one welcome.
items.exampleCN: hospes 涵盖同一份欢迎的两端。

items.example: Hospitium names the bond and the lodging.
items.exampleCN: hospitium 既指这层关系，也指寄宿的地方。

items.meaningCN: 表示「可以……的」的形容词语尾
items.example: The suffix -able makes hospitable from the stem.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 由词干构成 hospitable。

items.example: Hospitable is the base word.
items.exampleCN: hospitable 是基础词。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ity forms hospitality.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 hospitality。

items.example: Hospitality names the welcome itself.
items.exampleCN: hospitality 指欢迎本身。

items.example: Hospital began as a place of shelter for guests.
items.exampleCN: hospital 最初是收留客人的庇护所。

items.meaningCN: 表示「以……方式」的副词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ly forms inhospitably.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 inhospitably。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ness forms hospitableness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 hospitableness。

definition_zh: 不人道的；残忍的；无人性的；缺乏同情心的
definition_en: cruel and lacking in human kindness or sympathy, especially when treating people or animals harshly
core_image: 牢房外的人隔着铁栏冷眼旁观，里面的人毫无尊严
scene: 人们批评这种把动物关在狭小笼子里长途运输的做法很不人道。Critics called the practice of shipping animals in cramped crates inhumane.
sceneCN: 这里 inhumane 是「不人道的、残忍的」（第 1 个义项：对人缺乏怜悯）；句意：人们批评这种把动物关在狭小笼子里长途运输的做法很不人道。

pos.zh: 不人道的；残忍的；无人性的

derivatives.zh: 基础形容词 inhumane 加副词后缀 -ly，义为「不人道地」
同根名词，由拉丁语 humanitas（人性）加否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「残暴；残忍」
在 human 前加 in- 构成，义为「无人性的；非人的」，多指冷漠或超乎常情
拉丁语 humanitas 的英语形式，义为「人性；人类」，是不人道的反面
由 humane 加 -ly 构成，义为「仁慈地；人道地」，与 inhumane 语义相反

senses.title: Cruel treatment of people
senses.definition: treating people with cruelty and without the kindness that human beings are owed
senses.definitionCN: 以残酷的方式对待他人，不给其应得的善意与尊重
senses.example: The prison was criticized for its inhumane treatment of detainees.
senses.exampleCN: 这座监狱因对被拘留者的不人道待遇而受到批评。
senses.why: The prefix in- takes away the kindness built into humane, so the first sense is the absence of fellow feeling toward people.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 in- 把 humane 中的善意整个拿走，所以第一个义项就是对人失去了同类之情。

senses.title: Lacking pity for animals
senses.definition: causing suffering to animals without any sense of pity
senses.definitionCN: 让动物遭受痛苦而毫无怜悯之心
senses.example: Farmers who keep animals in these conditions are being inhumane.
senses.exampleCN: 以这种条件饲养动物的农户是不人道的。
senses.why: Pity is a human quality, and denying it to creatures that feel pain is the same loss of kindness applied outward.
senses.whyCN: 怜悯本是人之所以为人的品质，把它从能感觉痛苦的动物身上抽走，是同一种善意缺失向外延伸。

senses.title: Systems that deny dignity
senses.definition: describing rules, conditions, or systems that strip people of dignity
senses.definitionCN: 形容剥夺人的尊严的规则、条件或制度
senses.example: The new rules on overtime have been described as an inhumane system.
senses.exampleCN: 新的加班规定被形容为一套不人道的制度。
senses.why: When mechanical rules replace human care, the same coldness spreads from one act to a whole system.
senses.whyCN: 当机械的规则取代了人的关怀，这种冷漠就从某一次行为蔓延到整个制度。

senses.title: Without human warmth
senses.definition: showing no warmth or emotional response where kindness is expected
senses.definitionCN: 在本该给予温情时毫无热度与情感回应
senses.example: His inhumane silence when she was crying shocked the room.
senses.exampleCN: 她哭的时候他那不近人情的沉默让全屋人震惊。
senses.why: If kindness is the warmth that makes someone humane, its loss shows up first as a cold absence of response.
senses.whyCN: 如果善意就是让人成为「有人情味」的温度，那它的丢失首先表现为一种冷冰冰的无回应。

senses.title: Used to condemn an action
senses.definition: used mainly as a moral judgement when condemning an action or policy
senses.definitionCN: 主要用于对某种行为或政策作出道德评判与谴责
senses.example: It is inhumane to send elderly patients home with no care plan.
senses.exampleCN: 让老年病人毫无照护计划地回家是不人道的。
senses.why: A word that names the loss of human kindness easily turns into a moral verdict, so inhumane often carries a protest.
senses.whyCN: 一个直指「人性缺失」的词很容易变成道德判决，所以 inhumane 往往带着抗议的语气。

intro.en: Inhumane is built in English from the negative prefix in- and humane, a word that goes back through French to Latin humanus, of man.
intro.cn: inhumane 是英语中由否定前缀 in- 加 humane 构成的词；humane 经法语来自拉丁语 humanus（人的）。

items.en: Humanus means belonging to a man and, by extension, kind toward others.
items.cn: humanus 意为「人的」，引申为「对人有善意的」。

items.en: Humain carries both the human and the gentle sense.
items.cn: 古法语 humain 兼有「人的」与「温和的」两义。

items.en: Humane appears with the doubled ending, and humane and human begin to split in spelling.
items.cn: 中古英语出现 humane 这种双写词尾的拼法，humane 与 human 的拼写开始分化。

items.en: Humane settles on the sense of kind and compassionate, setting up a clear contrast pair.
items.cn: 近代英语中 humane 固定为「仁慈的、有同情心的」，与 human 形成清楚对立。

items.en: Inhumane is formed by adding in- to humane, with the stress kept on the last syllable as in humane.
items.cn: 十八至十九世纪，humane 前加否定前缀 in- 构成 inhumane，重音仍留在末音节（与 humane 一致）。

items.en: Inhumane is now used mainly for cruelty toward people and animals, while inhuman often describes coldness or something not human.
items.cn: 现代英语中 inhumane 主要用来指对人与动物的残忍，inhuman 多指冷漠或非人之物。

note.en: Inhumane belongs to the human family with in- negation, and it sits beside other words for cruelty.
note.cn: inhumane 属于带否定前缀 in- 的 human 词族，并与其它表示残酷的词相邻。

entries.definition: kind and showing compassion toward people or animals
entries.definitionCN: 仁慈的；有人情味的，与 inhumane 相对

entries.definition: lacking normal human feelings, or not belonging to human kind
entries.definitionCN: 无人性的；非人的，与 inhumane 只差一个字母，但重音位置不同

entries.definition: great cruelty, or an act that lacks human feeling
entries.definitionCN: 残暴；缺乏人性的行为，是 inhumane 的同源名词

entries.definition: in a kind and compassionate way
entries.definitionCN: 以仁慈、人道的方式，与 inhumane 语义相反

entries.definition: extremely violent and cruel
entries.definitionCN: 残忍的；野蛮的，强调暴力程度

entries.definition: showing no pity at all
entries.definitionCN: 无情的；毫不留情的，重点在缺乏怜悯

entries.definition: extremely cruel and uncivilized
entries.definitionCN: 野蛮的；凶残的，强调未开化

normalIntro.en: Inhumane is humane with a door shut in front of it: the prefix in- marks the lack of human kindness.
normalIntro.cn: inhumane 就是在 humane 前面关上一道门：前缀 in- 表示缺少人间温情。

normal.en: Keep humane and human apart: humane means kind, human means of people.
normal.cn: 先分清 humane 与 human：humane 是「仁慈的」，human 是「人的」。

normal.en: The prefix in- need not mean in; here it works like not or without.
normal.cn: 前缀 in- 不一定表示「进入」，这里相当于 not 或 without。

normal.en: The stress stays at the end, in-hue-MAINE, the same as humane.
normal.cn: 重音落在末尾，读作 in-hue-MAINE，与 humane 一致。

normal.en: Read the in- of inhumane as a denial, not as the inward in- of inject or inland.
normal.cn: inhumane 的 in- 要按「否定」理解，而不是 inject 中「向内」或 inland 中「内部」的意思。

normal.en: Humane in human rights reminds you of the kindness that inhumane denies.
normal.cn: 人权一词中的 humane 意味提醒你，inhumane 否定的正是这份善意。

abstract.en: Picture a guard watching prisoners in the rain through an iron fence.
abstract.cn: 想象一个看守隔着铁栅栏，看囚犯在雨里受冻。

abstract.en: Picture a narrow cage as long as a truck, with no room to turn around.
abstract.cn: 想象一个只有卡车车厢那么窄的笼子，里面的动物连转身都做不到。

abstract.en: Picture a form stamped in ink, where people become mere numbers.
abstract.cn: 想象一张墨迹盖下的表格，活生生的人被压缩成一个个编号。

examples.en: The report condemns the inhumane treatment of migrant workers.
examples.cn: 报告谴责了对移民工人的不人道待遇。

examples.en: Keeping wild animals in tiny cages for years is inhumane.
examples.cn: 把野生动物常年关在狭小的笼子里是不人道的。

examples.en: Some critics say the ban is more inhumane than the trade it aims to stop.
examples.cn: 一些批评者认为，这道禁令比它要阻止的交易更缺乏人道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬获民」——硬要占获别人的利益，对百姓毫不同情，就是不人道；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 humanus（人的）→ 古法语 humain → 中古英语 humane（仁慈的）→ 加否定前缀 in- 构成 inhumane（不人道的）。与 human、humanity、inhumanity 同族。

sensesIntro.en: From one core of denied human kindness, inhumane spreads from cruelty to people and animals, to cold systems, to an adjective of moral condemnation.
sensesIntro.cn: inhumane 从一个核心「被否定的同情心」出发，依次指向对人的残忍、对动物的残忍、冷酷的制度，最后成为一种道德谴责的形容词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone watching suffering through an iron fence and feeling nothing.
core.cn: 核心意象：有人隔着铁栅栏看着痛苦，却毫无触动。

branches.en: Cruelty toward people is the central documented sense.
branches.cn: 对人的残忍是主体义项，也是新闻与法规中最常见的用法。

branches.en: Animal welfare writing extends the same judgement to animals.
branches.cn: 动物福利文章把同一判断延伸到动物身上。

branches.en: When a rule or institution removes dignity, people call it inhumane.
branches.cn: 当某项规则或制度剥夺了人的尊严，人们称它不人道。

branches.en: Denying warmth to a person is both an act of cruelty and a tone of coldness.
branches.cn: 对人的冷漠既是残酷的行为，也是一种冷冰冰的态度。

branches.en: The word is most often used to judge and protest, not merely to describe.
branches.cn: 这个词最常用来评判与抗议，而不只是客观描述。

intro.en: Inhumane is the negative prefix in- plus humane, a word that runs through human, humanity, inhuman and humanely.
intro.cn: inhumane 由否定前缀 in- 加 humane 构成，humane 又串起 human、humanity、inhuman 与 humanely。

latinIntro.en: Latin humanus, of a man, gives the family; the in- that denies it is a Latin negative prefix as well.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 humanus（人的）是整个词族的源头，而否定的 in- 同样来自拉丁语否定前缀。

items.example: The prefix in- in inhumane means not.
items.exampleCN: inhumane 中的前缀 in- 表示「不」。

items.example: Humane is the base word.
items.exampleCN: humane（人道的）是基础词。

items.example: Human and humane split in meaning by the early modern period.
items.exampleCN: human 与 humane 在近代早期意义分化。

items.meaningCN: human 词族中 humane 的拼写标志
items.example: The final e separates humane from human.
items.exampleCN: 词尾的 e 使 humane 区别于 human。

items.example: The suffix -ly turns inhumane into an adverb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成副词形式。

items.example: Inhumanely describes cruel conduct.
items.exampleCN: inhumanely 描述残忍的行为方式。

items.example: The suffix -ity builds inhumanity.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 inhumanity。

items.example: Inhumanity names the quality itself.
items.exampleCN: inhumanity 指这种性质本身。

items.example: Inhuman is the shorter negative partner.
items.exampleCN: inhuman 是更短的否定形式。

items.example: Humanity is the positive root word.
items.exampleCN: humanity 是正面的同根词。

derivatives.zh: 不人道地
残暴；无人性
无人性的；非人的

definition_zh: 注射；注入；投入资金；注入活力或新元素
definition_en: to put a liquid or drug into the body with a needle, or to add money, energy, or a new element into a system
core_image: 针头刺入皮肤，药液被推进血管
scene: 护士卷起病人的袖子，把药液推进手臂的血管里。A nurse rolled up the patient sleeves and injected the medicine into the arm.
sceneCN: 这里 inject 是「注射、注入」（第 1 个义项：用针把药物注入体内）；句意：护士卷起病人的袖子，把药液推进手臂的血管里。

pos.zh: 注射；注入；投入；注入（活力、资金等）

derivatives.zh: 由 -ject 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「注射；注入物；投入」
动词 inject 加表示施动者的后缀 -or，义为「注射器；喷油嘴」
由 inject 加形容词后缀 -able 构成，义为「可注射的」
同根词，前缀 re-（回、向后）加 -ject（扔），义为「扔回去，拒绝」
同根词，前缀 e-（向外）加 -ject（扔），义为「弹出；驱逐」
同根词，前缀 pro-（向前）加 -ject（扔），义为「投射；计划」

senses.title: To put medicine into the body
senses.definition: to force a liquid drug into a person or animal with a needle or syringe
senses.definitionCN: 用针或注射器把液体药物强行注入人或动物体内
senses.example: The doctor injected a painkiller into her shoulder.
senses.exampleCN: 医生把止痛药注射进她的肩膀。
senses.why: The root -ject means to throw, and a needle throws a dose into the body.
senses.whyCN: 词根 -ject 意为「扔」，针头就是把一份药剂扔进身体里。

senses.title: To put money into a business
senses.definition: to provide money to a company, bank, or economy to support or revive it
senses.definitionCN: 向公司、银行或经济体提供资金以支持或挽救它
senses.example: The government injected billions into the struggling banks.
senses.exampleCN: 政府向陷入困境的银行注入了数十亿资金。
senses.why: Money pushed into a failing system works like a dose of medicine thrown in to revive it.
senses.whyCN: 把钱推进运转不良的系统，就像扔进一剂药把它救活，与注射同构。

senses.title: To fill a system with fuel or fluid
senses.definition: to force fuel or liquid into an engine, pipe, or container under pressure
senses.definitionCN: 在压力下把燃料或液体注入发动机、管道或容器
senses.example: Fuel is injected directly into the cylinder.
senses.exampleCN: 燃料被直接喷注进气缸。
senses.why: The medical image becomes mechanical: a pump throws fuel into a chamber, just as a needle throws fluid into a vein.
senses.whyCN: 医学意象变成机械意象：泵把燃料抛进燃烧室，正如针把药液抛进血管。

senses.title: To add energy or liveliness
senses.definition: to bring new energy, excitement, or humour into something dull
senses.definitionCN: 给沉闷的事物带来新的活力、兴奋或幽默
senses.example: Her jokes injected some fun into a very long meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 她的笑话给一场冗长的会议注入了几分乐趣。
senses.why: Anything that suddenly revives a tired thing is thrown in the way a liquid is; energy behaves like a dose.
senses.whyCN: 凡能让疲惫事物瞬间复苏的东西，都像液体一样被「扔进去」；活力被当成一剂药。

senses.title: To add a new element
senses.definition: to introduce a new idea, sound, or feature into a piece of work or discussion
senses.definitionCN: 把新的想法、声音或特色引入作品或讨论之中
senses.example: The producer injected a drum loop into the old song.
senses.exampleCN: 制作人给这首老歌加入了鼓点循环。
senses.why: The gesture of throwing in extends to ideas and sounds, which are introduced the way a substance is injected.
senses.whyCN: 「扔进去」的动作也被借给想法与声音，它们像某种物质一样被引入。

intro.en: Inject comes from the Latin verb inicere, to throw in, built from in- plus iacere, to throw; English borrowed it from the Latin participle in-iectus.
intro.cn: inject 来自拉丁语动词 inicere（扔进去），由 in-（向内）与 iacere（扔）构成；英语借自拉丁语分词词干 in-iectus。

items.en: A reconstructed root for to throw, often written yet, underlies iacere; the reconstruction is standard but not certain in every detail.
items.cn: iacere（扔）上溯到一个重构的原始印欧语词根（常写作 yet，意为「扔」）；这一重构形式学界通用，但细节并非没有争议。

items.en: Iacere means to throw, and prefix iacere with in- to get inicere, to throw in.
items.cn: 拉丁语 iacere 意为「扔」，加前缀 in- 组成 inicere，意为「扔进去」。

items.en: Latin medical and rhetorical writers use inicere for throwing something into a body or a speech.
items.cn: 四至五世纪，拉丁医学与修辞作者已用 inicere 表示把某物投入身体或言论之中。

items.en: The past participle stem in-iectus gives the t of the English form, and the prefix is pronounced with its letter n intact.
items.cn: 过去分词词干 in-iectus 带来英语形式里的字母 t，而 in- 中的 n 在英语中完整读出。

items.en: Inject enters English in the 1600s, first for throwing in fluids or ideas, and the medical sense grows with modern medicine.
items.cn: 十七世纪中叶，inject 进入英语，最初指把液体或想法投入；医学义随现代医学的发展而壮大。

items.en: Modern English extends inject from medicine to money, engines, and energy, all keeping the throw-in image.
items.cn: 现代英语把 inject 从医学扩展到资金、发动机与活力，全都保留「扔进去」的意象。

note.en: Inject shares the -ject throw family with project and reject, and it is close to words about giving medicine.
note.cn: inject 与 project、reject 同属「扔」的 -ject 词族，并与表示给药的一类词相邻。

entries.definition: the act of putting medicine in with a needle, or the money that is put in
a device that forces fuel or liquid into an engine
entries.definitionCN: 喷油嘴；注射器，指执行注入的装置

entries.definition: to throw something forward, such as an image or a plan
entries.definitionCN: 投射；规划，前缀 pro- 表向前，与 -ject 同根

entries.definition: to throw something against or in the way as a protest
entries.definitionCN: 反对，字面为「扔到对面去」，同根异前缀

entries.definition: to give a vaccine to protect against a disease
entries.definitionCN: 接种疫苗，是 inject 在预防医学中的常见场景

entries.definition: to add a quality or feeling into something gradually
entries.definitionCN: 注入、灌输（品质、情感），比 inject 更强调缓慢渗透

entries.definition: to force liquid, gas, or money into a place with a pump
entries.definitionCN: 泵入；大量投入，是 inject 的口语化说法

normalIntro.en: Inject keeps the Latin gesture of throwing: the prefix in- says inward, and the root -ject throws the dose in.
normalIntro.cn: inject 保留拉丁语「扔」的动作：前缀 in- 指出方向是「向内」，词根 -ject 把剂量扔进去。

normal.en: The root -ject means to throw, as in reject and eject.
normal.cn: 词根 -ject 意为「扔」，reject 和 eject 里都是它。

normal.en: Reject throws back, eject throws out, inject throws in.
normal.cn: reject 是扔回去，eject 是扔出去，inject 是扔进去。

normal.en: Injection is the noun, injector is the device that does it.
normal.cn: injection 是名词形式，injector 是执行注入的装置。

normal.en: In finance, inject money into a company just as a doctor injects a drug.
normal.cn: 财经语境里 inject money into a company，正如医生给病人注射药物。

normal.en: The medical verb is transitive, so inject needs an object: inject a drug, not simply inject.
normal.cn: 这是及物动词，后面要带宾语：inject a drug，而不单用 inject。

abstract.en: Picture a plunger pushing clear liquid through a thin steel needle.
abstract.cn: 想象活塞把清亮的液体推过一根细钢针。

abstract.en: Picture a hypodermic of banknotes shot into a shaking balance sheet.
abstract.cn: 想象一支里面装着钞票的针管，被扎进一张发抖的资产负债表。

abstract.en: Picture a hand throwing a small glowing dose deep into a dark chamber.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把一小团发光的剂量扔进幽暗的燃烧室。

examples.en: The nurse injected the vaccine into his left arm.
examples.cn: 护士把疫苗注射进他的左臂。

examples.en: The state will inject fresh capital into its railway network.
examples.cn: 该州将向铁路网注入新的资本。

examples.en: Fuel is injected into the engine under very high pressure.
examples.cn: 燃料在极高压下被喷注进发动机。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因救」——一针药推进去，因它获救；谐音只帮助记住读音，与真实词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（向内）+ iacere（扔）→ inicere（扔进去）→ 英语借自分词词干 in-iectus。同族词有 project（向前扔）、reject（扔回去）、eject（扔出去）、object（扔到对面）。

sensesIntro.en: From one gesture of throwing something inward, inject moves from medicine to money, to engines, to energy, to new ideas in a piece of work.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一个「往里扔」的动作出发，inject 先从医学走到资金，再走到发动机，然后是活力，最后是作品中引入的新元素。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a needle throwing a dose inward into the body.
core.cn: 核心意象：针头把一剂药剂往里扔进身体。

branches.en: The medical sense is the most concrete and most frequent.
branches.cn: 医学义最具体，也是出现频率最高的义项。

branches.en: Money is treated as a liquid dose injected into a weak organisation.
branches.cn: 资金被当成液体药剂，注入虚弱的机构。

branches.en: In engines the same throwing becomes a jet of fuel under pressure.
branches.cn: 在发动机里，同一个「扔」变成了压力下的燃料射流。

branches.en: Capital and energy are both things added from outside to revive what is tired.
branches.cn: 资本和活力都是从外部加入、用来让疲惫之物复苏的东西。

branches.en: Humour and new ideas are injected into dull or dull-sounding material.
branches.cn: 幽默与新点子被注入沉闷或平淡的内容里。

intro.en: Inject is the prefix in- plus the Latin root -ject, to throw, which also runs through project, reject, eject and object.
intro.cn: inject 是前缀 in- 加拉丁词根 -ject（扔），同族还有 project、reject、eject 与 object。

latinIntro.en: Latin iacere means to throw, and its participle stem iectus supplies the ject seen in the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 iacere 意为「扔」，其分词词干 iectus 提供了英语中可见的 ject。

items.example: The prefix in- marks direction in inject.
items.exampleCN: inject 中的前缀 in- 表示方向向内。

items.example: The root -ject appears in a whole family of verbs.
items.exampleCN: 词根 -ject 出现在一整族动词里。

items.example: Iacere is the Latin source of the root.
items.exampleCN: iacere 是该词根的拉丁语源头。

items.example: Inicere is the direct Latin ancestor.
items.exampleCN: inicere 是直接的拉丁语祖词。

items.example: The suffix -ion forms injection.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 构成 injection。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does
items.meaningCN: 做某事的人或物（施动后缀）
items.example: The suffix -or forms injector.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -or 构成 injector。

items.example: The suffix -able forms injectable.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成 injectable。

items.example: Pro- plus -ject gives project.
items.exampleCN: pro- 加 -ject 构成 project。

items.example: Re- plus -ject gives reject.
items.exampleCN: re- 加 -ject 构成 reject。

items.example: E- plus -ject gives eject.
items.exampleCN: e- 加 -ject 构成 eject。
